`sustainable aviation fuel' means liquid fuel, the portion of which is not kerosene, which is sold for use in an aircraft and which-- ``(i) meets the requirements of-- ``(I) ASTM International Standard D7566, or ``(II) the Fischer Tropsch provisions of ASTM International Standard D1655, Annex A1, and ``(ii) is not derived from palm fatty acid distillates or petroleum. ``(4) Sale.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the transportation fuel is sold in a manner described in this paragraph if such fuel is sold by the taxpayer to an unrelated person-- ``(A) for use by such person in the production of a fuel mixture, ``(B) for use by such person in a trade or business, or ``(C) who sells such fuel at retail to another person and places such fuel in the fuel tank of such other person. ``(5) Rounding.--If any amount determined under paragraph (1) is not a multiple of 1 cent, such amount shall be rounded to the nearest cent. ``(b) Emissions Factors.-- ``(1) <<NOTE: Determinations.>> Emissions factor.-- ``(A) Calculation.-- ``(i) In general.--The emissions factor of a transportation fuel shall be an amount equal to the quotient of-- ``(I) an amount equal to-- [[Page 136 STAT. 1999]] ``(aa) 50 kilograms of CO<INF>2</INF>e per mmBTU, minus ``(bb) the emissions rate for such fuel, divided by ``(II) 50 kilograms of CO<INF>2</INF>e per mmBTU. ``(B) Establishment of emissions rate.-- ``(i) <<NOTE: Publication.>> In general.-- Subject to clauses (ii) and (iii), the Secretary shall annually publish a table which sets forth the emissions rate for similar types and categories of transportation fuels based on the amount of lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions (as described in section 211(o)(1)(H) of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7545(o)(1)(H)), as in effect on the date of the enactment of this section) for such fuels, expressed as kilograms of CO<INF>2</INF>e per mmBTU, which a taxpayer shall use for purposes of this section. ``(ii) Non-aviation fuel.--In the case of any transportation fuel which is not a sustainable aviation fuel, the lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions of such fuel shall be based on the most recent determinations under the Greenhouse gases, Regulated Emissions, and Energy use in Transportation model developed by Argonne National Laboratory, or a successor model (as determined by the Secretary). ``(iii) Aviation fuel.--In the case of any transportation fuel which is a sustainable aviation fuel, the lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions of such fuel shall be determined in accordance with-- ``(I) the most recent Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation which has been adopted by the International Civil Aviation Organization with the agreement of the United States, or ``(II) any similar methodology which satisfies the criteria under section 211(o)(1)(H) of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7545(o)(1)(H)), as in effect on the date of enactment of this section. ``(C) Rounding of emissions rate.-- ``(i) In general.--Subject to clause (ii), the Secretary may round the emissions rates under subparagraph (B) to the nearest multiple of 5 kilograms of CO<INF>2</INF>e per mmBTU. ``(ii) Exception.--In the case of an emissions rate that is between 2.5 kilograms of CO<INF>2</INF>e per mmBTU and -2.5 kilograms of CO<INF>2</INF>e per mmBTU, the Secretary may round such rate to zero. ``(D) Provisional emissions rate.--In the case of any transportation fuel for which an emissions rate has not been established under subparagraph (B), a taxpayer producing such fuel may file a petition with the Secretary for determination of the emissions rate with respect to such fuel. ``(2) Rounding.--If any amount determined under paragraph (1)(A) is not a multiple of 0.1, such amount shall be rounded to the nearest multiple of 0.1. ``(c) Inflation Adjustment.-- [[Page 136 STAT. 2000]] ``(1) <<NOTE: Effective date.>> In general.--In the case of calendar years beginning after 2024, the 20 cent amount in subsection (a)(2)(A), the $1.00 amount in subsection (a)(2)(B), the 35 cent amount in subsection (a)(3)(A)(i), and the $1.75 amount in subsection (a)(3)(A)(ii) shall each be adjusted by multiplying such amount by the inflation adjustment factor for the calendar year in which the sale of the transportation fuel occurs. If any amount as increased under the preceding sentence is not a multiple of 1 cent, such amount shall be rounded to the nearest multiple of 1 cent. ``(2) <<NOTE: Determination. Publication.>> Inflation adjustment factor.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the inflation adjustment factor shall be the inflation adjustment factor determined and published by the Secretary pursuant to section 45Y(c), determined by substituting `calendar year 2022' for `calendar year 1992' in paragraph (3) thereof. ``(d) Definitions.--In this section: ``(1) mmBTU.--The term `mmBTU' means 1,000,000 British thermal units. ``(2) CO<INF>2</INF>e.--The term `CO<INF>2</INF>e' means, with respect to any greenhouse gas, the equivalent carbon dioxide (as determined based on relative global warming potential). ``(3) Greenhouse gas.--The term `greenhouse gas' has the same meaning given that term under section 211(o)(1)(G) of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7545(o)(1)(G)), as in effect on the date of the enactment of this section. ``(4) Qualified facility.--The term `qualified facility'-- ``(A) means a facility used for the production of transportation fuels, and ``(B) does not include any facility for which one of the following credits is allowed under section 38 for the taxable year: ``(i) The credit for production of clean hydrogen under section 45V. ``(ii) The credit determined under section 46 to the extent that such credit is attributable to the energy credit determined under section 48 with respect to any specified clean hydrogen production facility for which an election is made under subsection (a)(15) of such section. ``(iii) The credit for carbon oxide sequestration under section 45Q. ``(5) Transportation fuel.-- ``(A) In general.--The term `transportation fuel' means a fuel which-- ``(i) is suitable for use as a fuel in a highway vehicle or aircraft, ``(ii) has an emissions rate which is not greater than 50 kilograms of CO<INF>2</INF>e per mmBTU, and ``(iii) is not derived from coprocessing an applicable material (or materials derived from an applicable material) with a feedstock which is not biomass. ``(B) Definitions.--In this paragraph-- ``(i) Applicable material.--The term `applicable material' means-- ``(I) monoglycerides, diglycerides, and triglycerides, ``(II) free fatty acids, and [[Page 136 STAT. 2001]] ``(III) fatty acid esters. ``(ii) Biomass.--The term `biomass' has the same meaning given such term in section 45K(c)(3). ``(e) <<NOTE: Deadline. Determination.>> Guidance.--Not later than January 1, 2025, the Secretary shall issue guidance regarding implementation of this section, including calculation of emissions factors for transportation fuel, the table described in subsection (b)(1)(B)(i), and the determination of clean fuel production credits under this section. ``(f) <<NOTE: Applicability.>> Special Rules.-- ``(1) Only registered production in the united states taken into account.-- ``(A) In general.--No clean fuel production credit shall be determined under subsection (a) with respect to any transportation fuel unless-- ``(i) the taxpayer-- ``(I) is registered as a producer of clean fuel under section 4101 at the time of production, and ``(II) in the case of any transportation fuel which is a sustainable aviation fuel, provides-- ``(aa) <<NOTE: Certification.>> certification (in such form and manner as the Secretary shall prescribe) from an unrelated party demonstrating compliance with-- ``(AA) any general requirements, supply chain traceability requirements, and information transmission requirements established under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation described in subclause (I) of subsection (b)(1)(B)(iii), or ``(BB) in the case of any methodology described in subclause (II) of such subsection, requirements similar to the requirements described in subitem (AA), and ``(bb) such other information with respect to such fuel as the Secretary may require for purposes of carrying out this section, and ``(ii) such fuel is produced in the United States. ``(B) <<NOTE: Definition.>> United states.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `United States' includes any possession of the United States. ``(2) Production attributable to the taxpayer.--In the case of a facility in which more than 1 person has an ownership interest, except to the extent provided in regulations prescribed by the Secretary, production from the facility shall be allocated among such persons in proportion to their respective ownership interests in the gross sales from such facility. ``(3) Related persons.--Persons shall be treated as related to each other if such persons would be treated as a single employer under the regulations prescribed under section 52(b). In the case of a corporation which is a member of an affiliated group of corporations filing a consolidated return, such corporation shall be treated as selling fuel to an unrelated person if such fuel is sold to such a person by another member of such group. [[Page 136 STAT. 2002]] ``(4) Pass-thru in the case of estates and trusts.--Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary, rules similar to the rules of subsection (d) of section 52 shall apply. ``(5) Allocation of credit to patrons of agricultural cooperative.--Rules similar to the rules of section 45Y(g)(6) shall apply. ``(6) Prevailing wage requirements.-- ``(A) In general.--Subject to subparagraph (B), rules similar to the rules of section 45(b)(7) shall apply. ``(B) Special rule for facilities placed in service before january 1, 2025.--For purposes of subparagraph (A), in the case of any qualified facility placed in service before January 1, 2025-- ``(i) clause (i) of section 45(b)(7)(A) shall not apply, and ``(ii) clause (ii) of such section shall be applied by substituting `with respect to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024, for which the credit is allowed under this section' for `with respect to any taxable year, for any portion of such taxable year which is within the period described in subsection (a)(2)(A)(ii)'. ``(7) Apprenticeship requirements.--Rules similar to the rules of section 45(b)(8) shall apply. ``(g) Termination.--This section shall not apply to transportation fuel sold after December 31, 2027.''. (b) Conforming Amendments.-- (1) Section 25C(d)(3), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, <<NOTE: 26 USC 25.>> is amended-- (A) in subparagraph (A), by striking ``and'' at the end, (B) in subparagraph (B), by striking the period at the end and inserting ``, and'', and (C) by adding at the end the following new subparagraph: ``(C) transportation fuel (as defined in section 45Z(d)(5)).''. (2) Section 30C(c)(1)(B), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by adding at the end the following new clause: ``(iv) Any transportation fuel (as defined in section 45Z(d)(5)).''. (3) Section 38(b), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended-- (A) in paragraph (38), by striking ``plus'' at the end, (B) in paragraph (39), by striking the period at the end and inserting ``, plus'', and (C) by adding at the end the following new paragraph: ``(40) the clean fuel production credit determined under section 45Z(a).''. (4) The table of sections for subpart D of part IV of subchapter A of chapter 1, as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, <<NOTE: 26 USC 38 prec.>> is amended by adding at the end the following new item: ``Sec. 45Z. Clean fuel production credit.''. [[Page 136 STAT. 2003]] (5) Section 4101(a)(1), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, <<NOTE: 26 USC 4101.>> is amended by inserting ``every person producing a fuel eligible for the clean fuel production credit (pursuant to section 45Z),'' after ``section 6426(k)(3)),''. claim_source_map.passage: (e) Alcohol, biodiesel, alternative fuel, or sustainable aviation fuel Except as provided in subsection (k)— (1) Used to produce a mixture If any person produces a mixture described in section 6426 in such person's trade or business, the Secretary shall pay (without interest) to such person an amount equal to the alcohol fuel mixture credit or the biodiesel mixture credit or the alternative fuel mixture credit or the sustainable aviation fuel mixture credit with respect to such mixture. (2) Alternative fuel If any person sells or uses an alternative fuel (as defined in section 6426(d)(2)) for a purpose described in section 6426(d)(1) in such person's trade or business, the Secretary shall pay (without interest) to such person an amount equal to the alternative fuel credit with respect to such fuel. (3) Coordination with other repayment provisions No amount shall be payable under paragraph (1) or (2) with respect to any mixture or alternative fuel with respect to which an amount is allowed as a credit under section 6426. (4) Registration requirement for alternative fuels The Secretary shall not make any payment under this subsection to any person with respect to any alternative fuel credit or alternative fuel mixture credit unless the person is registered under section 4101. (5) Limitation to fuels with connection to the United States No amount shall be payable under paragraph (1) or (2) with respect to any mixture or alternative fuel if credit is not allowed with respect to such mixture or alternative fuel by reason of section 6426(i). (6) Termination This subsection shall not apply with respect to— (A) any alcohol fuel mixture (as defined in section 6426(b)(3)) sold or used after December 31, 2011, (B) any biodiesel mixture (as defined in section 6426(c)(3)) sold or used after December 31, 2024, (C) any alternative fuel (as defined in section 6426(d)(2)) sold or used after December 31, 2024, (D) any alternative fuel mixture (as defined in section 6426(e)(2)) sold or used after December 31, 2011, and (E) any qualified mixture of sustainable aviation fuel (as defined in section 6426(k)(3)) 1 sold or used after December 31, 2024.

claim_source_map.passage: (i) Time for filing claims; period covered (1) General rule Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, not more than one claim may be filed under subsection (a), (b), (c), (d), (h), (l), (m), or (o) by any person with respect to fuel used during his taxable year; and no claim shall be allowed under this paragraph with respect to fuel used during any taxable year unless filed by the purchaser not later than the time prescribed by law for filing a claim for credit or refund of overpayment of income tax for such taxable year. For purposes of this paragraph, a person's taxable year shall be his taxable year for purposes of subtitle A. (2) Exceptions (A) In general If, at the close of any quarter of the taxable year of any person, at least $750 is payable in the aggregate under subsections (a), (b), (d), (h), (l), (m), and (o) of this section and section 6421 to such person with respect to fuel used during— (i) such quarter, or (ii) any prior quarter (for which no other claim has been filed) during such taxable year, a claim may be filed under this section with respect to such fuel. (B) Time for filing claim No claim filed under this paragraph shall be allowed unless filed during the first quarter following the last quarter included in the claim. (C) Nonapplication of paragraph This paragraph shall not apply to any fuel used solely in any off-highway business use described in section 6421(e)(2)(C). (3) Special rule for mixture credits and the alternative fuel credit (A) In general A claim may be filed under subsection (e)(1) by any person with respect to a mixture described in section 6426 or under subsection (e)(2) by any person with respect to an alternative fuel (as defined in section 6426(d)(2)) for any period— (i) for which $200 or more is payable under such subsection (e)(1) or (e)(2), and (ii) which is not less than 1 week. In the case of an electronic claim, this subparagraph shall be applied without regard to clause (i). (B) Payment of claim Notwithstanding subsection (e)(1) or (e)(2), if the Secretary has not paid pursuant to a claim filed under this section within 45 days of the date of the filing of such claim (20 days in the case of an electronic claim), the claim shall be paid with interest from such date determined by using the overpayment rate and method under section 6621. (C) Time for filing claim No claim filed under this paragraph shall be allowed unless filed on or before the last day of the first quarter following the earliest quarter included in the claim. (4) Special rule for vendor refunds (A) In general A claim may be filed under paragraph (4)(C) or (5) of subsection (l) by any person with respect to fuel sold by such person for any period— (i) for which $200 or more ($100 or more in the case of kerosene) is payable under paragraph (4)(C) or (5) of subsection (l), and (ii) which is not less than 1 week. Notwithstanding subsection (l)(1), paragraph (3)(B) shall apply to claims filed under subsections (b)(4), (l)(4)(C)(ii), and (l)(5). (B) Time for filing claim No claim filed under this paragraph shall be allowed unless filed on or before the last day of the first quarter following the earliest quarter included in the claim. (j) Applicable laws (1) In general All provisions of law, including penalties, applicable in respect of the taxes imposed by sections 4041 and 4081 shall, insofar as applicable and not inconsistent with this section, apply in respect of the payments provided for in this section to the same extent as if such payments constituted refunds of overpayments of the tax so imposed. (2) Examination of books and witnesses For the purpose of ascertaining the correctness of any claim made under this section, or the correctness of any payment made in respect of any such claim, the Secretary shall have the authority granted by paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of section 7602(a) (relating to examination of books and witnesses) as if the claimant were the person liable for tax. (k) Income tax credit in lieu of payment (1) Persons not subject to income tax Payment shall be made under this section only to— (A) the United States or an agency or instrumentality thereof, a State, a political subdivision of a State, or any agency or instrumentality of one or more States or political subdivisions, or (B) an organization exempt from tax under section 501(a) (other than an organization required to make a return of the tax imposed under subtitle A for its taxable year). (2) Exception Paragraph (1) shall not apply to a payment of a claim filed under paragraph (2), (3), or (4) of subsection (i). (3) Allowance of credit against income tax For allowances of credit against the income tax imposed by subtitle A for fuel used or resold by the purchaser, see section 34.

United States Code, 2024 Edition Title 26 - INTERNAL REVENUE CODE Subtitle D - Miscellaneous Excise Taxes CHAPTER 32 - MANUFACTURERS EXCISE TAXES Subchapter A - Automotive and Related Items PART III - PETROLEUM PRODUCTS Subpart B - Special Provisions Applicable to Fuels Tax Sec. 4101 - Registration and bond From the U.S. Government Publishing Office, www.gpo.gov §4101. Registration and bond (a) Registration (1) In general Every person required by the Secretary to register under this section with respect to the tax imposed by section 4041(a) or 4081, every person producing or importing biodiesel (as defined in section 40A(d)(1)) or alcohol (as defined in section 6426(b)(4)(A)), every person producing or importing sustainable aviation fuel (as defined in section 40B), every person producing a fuel eligible for the clean fuel production credit (pursuant to section 45Z), and every person producing second generation biofuel (as defined in section 40(b)(6)(E)) shall register with the Secretary at such time, in such form and manner, and subject to such terms and conditions, as the Secretary may by regulations prescribe. A registration under this section may be used only in accordance with regulations prescribed under this section. (2) Registration of persons within foreign trade zones, etc. The Secretary shall require registration by any person which— (A) operates a terminal or refinery within a foreign trade zone or within a customs bonded storage facility, or (B) holds an inventory position with respect to a taxable fuel in such a terminal. (3) Display of registration Every operator of a vessel required by the Secretary to register under this section shall display proof of registration through an identification device prescribed by the Secretary on each vessel used by such operator to transport any taxable fuel. (4) Registration of persons extending credit on certain exempt sales of fuel The Secretary shall require registration by any person which— (A) extends credit by credit card to any ultimate purchaser described in subparagraph (C) or (D) of section 6416(b)(2) for the purchase of taxable fuel upon which tax has been imposed under section 4041 or 4081, and (B) does not collect the amount of such tax from such ultimate purchaser. (5) Reregistration in event of change in ownership Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary, a person (other than a corporation the stock of which is regularly traded on an established securities market) shall be required to reregister under this section if after a transaction (or series of related transactions) more than 50 percent of ownership interests in, or assets of, such person are held by persons other than persons (or persons related thereto) who held more than 50 percent of such interests or assets before the transaction (or series of related transactions). (b) Bonds and liens (1) In general Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary, the Secretary may require, as a condition of permitting any person to be registered under subsection (a), that such person— (A) give a bond in such sum as the Secretary determines appropriate, and (B) agree to the imposition of a lien— (i) on such property (or rights to property) of such person used in the trade or business for which the registration is sought, or (ii) with the consent of such person, on any other property (or rights to property) of such person as the Secretary determines appropriate. Rules similar to the rules of section 6323 shall apply to the lien imposed pursuant to this paragraph. (2) Release or discharge of lien If a lien is imposed pursuant to paragraph (1), the Secretary shall issue a certificate of discharge or a release of such lien in connection with a transfer of the property if there is furnished to the Secretary (and accepted by him) a bond in such sum as the Secretary determines appropriate or the transferor agrees to the imposition of a substitute lien under paragraph (1)(B) in such sum as the Secretary determines appropriate. The Secretary shall respond to any request to discharge or release a lien imposed pursuant to paragraph (1) in connection with a transfer of property not later than 90 days after the date the request for such a discharge or release is made. (c) Denial, revocation, or suspension of registration Rules similar to the rules of section 4222(c) shall apply to registration under this section. (d) Information reporting The Secretary may require— (1) information reporting by any person registered under this section, and (2) information reporting by such other persons as the Secretary deems necessary to carry out this part. Any person who is required to report under this subsection and who has 25 or more reportable transactions in a month shall file such report in electronic format. house:119:1:190.short_description: H.R.1 Senate replacement: selected border, detention and asylum, employment-authorization and selected sponsor/enforcement fees
house:119:1:190.compact_description: Selected Senate H.R. 1 provisions would fund border infrastructure and detention, set fiscal 2025 asylum filing/pending fee floors of $100 each and specified asylum/parole/TPS employment-authorization initial/renewal fee floors of $550/$275, with distinct duration and termination rules. This is a whole-replacement concurrence choice, with qualifications.
house:119:1:190.meaning:
This July3 House concurrence concerns the Senate's July1 EAS, which strikes all after the first word and replaces the earlier H.R.1 text. It is the complete multi-domain reconciliation replacement, not a second passage of the unchanged House bill or a separate vote on its Immigration components. Selected Immigration highlights here concern border infrastructure, detention and asylum fees; other immigration-related benefits, taxes, employment authorization, child-sponsor, reimbursement and enforcement provisions are not exhaustively described. Section90001 would appropriate an additional $46.55billion for fiscal2025 to CBP, available until September30,2029, for new/replacement primary, waterborne and secondary barriers, access roads, detection attributes and ground preparation for CBP operations and barrier construction/maintenance. The different House60001 accounts are not silently used to define this replacement amount or its purposes. Section90003 would appropriate an additional $45billion for fiscal2025 to ICE, available until September30,2029, for single-adult alien detention and family residential-center capacity. Aliens MAY be detained at family centers pending an INA removal decision and, if ordered removed, until removal. Single-adult detention standards are set in the Secretary's discretion CONSISTENT WITH APPLICABLE LAW. The family-center definition covers apprehended/encountered family units, including children who are not statutorily defined unaccompanied alien children, and does not reproduce the House's express regardless-of-State-licensing clause.6USC279(g)(2) requires no lawful immigration status, under18 age, and no US parent/legal guardian or none available for care/physical custody. Neither the capacity funding nor permission establishes automatic detention/removal of every alien, elimination of all legal constraints or actual operations. Section100002 requires an additional fee upon filing an asylum application. The fiscal2025 amount is the greater of $100 or the amount set by DHS/the Attorney General, as applicable, by rule; it cannot be waived/reduced. From fiscal2026 the prior fiscal-year fee is increased by the printed July-to-July CPI-U increment rounded down to a multiple of $10. Half of Attorney-General-filed receipts go to EOIR; half of DHS-filed receipts go to USCIS's existing Immigration Examinations Fee Account, retained/expended without further appropriation; uncredited receipts go to Treasury. This $100 filing floor differs from the House's $1,000 floor. Section100009 separately requires an additional fee for EACH CALENDAR YEAR an asylum application remains pending. Its fiscal2025 amount is the greater of $100 or a DHS rule amount, followed by the printed CPI-U annual adjustment with the increment rounded DOWN TO THE NEAREST DOLLAR; receipts go to Treasury and the fee cannot be waived/reduced. Do not transfer that rounding to the initial-filing fee or back to the House's differently printed yearly formula. Section100018 changes pre-vote INA208(d)(3)/8USC1158(d)(3) from MAY impose fees to SHALL and replaces the following cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory-fee language with preserved additional adjudication/naturalization-fee authority under286(m). The baseline already authorized asylum-consideration, employment-authorization and asylum-based adjustment fees;1356(m)/(n) govern existing account/cost-recovery context. No first-ever fee authority, new asylum eligibility test from that edit, specific implemented collection rule or actual payment is inferred. Employment-authorization fees are separate from asylum filing and annual pending-application fees. Senate100003 requires additional initial application fees for asylum applicants under1158(d)(2), paroled aliens andTPS employment-authorization applicants under1254a(a)(1)(B). Each fiscal2025 floor is$550 or a higher DHS rule amount, with no waiver/reduction and fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increments rounded down to$10. The asylum-initial subsection contains no House-style six-month duration sentence; it credits25percent of fees collected PURSUANT TO THIS SUBSECTION to USCIS's existing fee account, retained/expended without further appropriation with NOT LESS THAN50percent of the credited share for benefit-fraud detection/prevention, and sends the rest to Treasury. Parole/TPS initial fees go to Treasury; their initial authorizations last one year or the duration of parole/TPS respectively, whichever is shorter. Senate100010 and100012 set separate parole/TPS employment-authorization renewal/extension fiscal2025 fee floors of$275, possible higher DHS rule amounts and later CPI increments rounded down to$10. Each sends25percent to USCIS's existing fee account to retain/spend without further appropriation and the rest to Treasury; no waiver/reduction.100012 states one year or the duration of the designation ofTPS, whichever is shorter.100010 literally says employment authorization for each paroled alien, OR ANY RENEWAL OR EXTENSION OF SUCH PAROLE, shall be valid for one year or parole duration, whichever is shorter. Preserve this printed antecedent and leave its application unresolved; do not rewrite it into a new parole-eligibility rule or import House six-month text. Senate100011 imposes at least$275 for each asylum-based employment-authorization renewal/extension, with25percent credited to USCIS's existing fee account without further appropriation, the rest to Treasury and no waiver/reduction. It prints no annual CPI formula or House-style six-month limit. It retains the three termination points: immediately after asylum-officer denial unless referred to an immigration judge;30days after immigration-judge denial unless timely appealed to BIA; immediately after BIA denies an appeal of asylum denial. It does not reproduce the separate House70013(d) prohibition on later grants/renewals/extensions absent a FederalCourtOfAppeals remand. Absence of that House sentence does not establish unlimited permission or erase other law. The complete pre-vote1158(d)(2) already permits regulated asylum-based work authorization while denying entitlement and preserving a180day wait for applicants not otherwise eligible. Existing1254a(a)(1)(B)/(a)(2) authorizes employment throughout TPS. Document-validity clauses do not themselves terminate TPS, create first employment authority or establish individual eligibility. Existing1182(d)(5)(A)/(B) preserves case-by-case temporary humanitarian/significant-public-benefit parole subject to the printed statutory exceptions, including its refugee qualification and the distinction from admission; paying a fee does not supply parole or work permission. Senate100016 requires a fiscal2025 fee of at least$5,000, or a higher DHS rule amount, on an alien BOTH ordered removed in absentia under1229a(b)(5) AND subsequently arrested by ICE, with fiscal2026-onward CPI-U increments rounded down to$10. It does not apply if the order was rescinded under1229a(b)(5)(C).50percent goes to ICE's Detention and Removal Office Fee Account, retained/expended without further appropriation; the rest goes to Treasury. It expressly bars waiver/reduction. These fee conditions preserve the underlying notice/address/removability proof, rescission, exceptional-circumstances definition and motion-to-reopen stay in complete pre-vote1229a(b)(5)/(e) and1229(a); an actual order/arrest, new removal ground or denied legal review is not inferred. Senate100017 separately requires an additional fee from any INADMISSIBLE alien at the time the person is apprehended BETWEEN PORTS OF ENTRY. Its fiscal2025 floor is$5,000 or a higher DHS rule amount, with later CPI-U increments rounded down to$10. Unlike House70022, this operative sentence does not name CBP as the apprehending actor. It prints TWO proceeds clauses: subsection(c) sends50percent to ICE's Detention and Removal Office Fee Account for retention/spending without further appropriation and the remainder to Treasury; subsection(d) says ALL fees under the section go to Treasury. The exact EAS HTML and officialPDF pages827-828 both print these clauses. The candidate preserves the apparent allocation conflict and does not choose an operative distribution. No express no-waiver clause is printed in100017; do not import100016(e) or House70022(d), or infer that a waiver is available. These are exact between-port/inadmissibility and in-absentia-plus-ICE-arrest fee predicates, not all enforcement encounters or a fee-imposed finding that an alien actually met any predicate. Senate100004 adds a parole-entry fee with fiscal2025floor$1,000 or higher DHS rule amount, subsequent CPI-U increments rounded down to$10 and Treasury disposition. Its exceptions require the alien to establish the parole reason to DHS's satisfaction on an INDIVIDUAL,CASE-BY-CASE basis; its no-waiver clause expressly preserves those exceptions. The fee exceptions retain their actual predicates: a medical emergency with necessary treatment unavailable in the foreign state where the alien resides OR a life-threatening emergency with insufficient normal-visa time; the parent/legal guardian of such a medical-emergency MINOR; the alien needed in the US to donate an organ or tissue for transplant, with insufficient normal-visa time; a close family member in the United States whose death is imminent, when normal visa processing would prevent arriving while that person is alive; or seeking to attend a close family member's funeral, when normal visa processing would prevent arriving in the United States in time for it; an adopted child's urgent treatment needed before expected final adoption-related visa issuance while in the petitioner's legal custody; a LAWFUL INA245 adjustment applicant returning after temporary travel abroad; and a person returned to a contiguous country under235(b)(2)(C) paroled to attend the person's immigration hearing. The law-enforcement significant-public-benefit exception requires a DHS determination that significant public benefit has resulted or will result from the parole, BOTH assistance to the USGovernment AND presence required in that matter, PLUS at least one of inadmissibility, failure to meet nonimmigrant-admission eligibility, or insufficient normal-visa time; it is not every asserted public benefit. Senate exception9 instead requires that the alien HASBEENGRANTED the status of Cuban/Haitianentrant as defined inPL96-422Sec501(e). That complete definition distinguishes special Cuban/Haitianentrant-parole/subsequently-established special-status categories from OTHERCuban/Haitian nationals with the listed parole/no-other-status, removal-proceeding or pending-asylum alternatives AND no final,nonappealable,legally-enforceable removal order. Its status-at-assistance/services wording is preserved in the bound definition, not silently turned into proof of the fee-specific grant condition or a nationality-only exemption. Do not use the different House Cuba-residence/family-petition/program conjunction to define this replacement, or infer actual parole/fee exemption from nationality. Existing1182(d)(5) authority/statutory exceptions/non-admission distinction remain; paying or excepting a fee does not grant parole, admission or adjustment. Senate100005 requires an additional SIJapplication fee from ANYALIEN,PARENT,ORLEGALGUARDIAN of an alien applying under1101(a)(27)(J), with fiscal2025floor$250 or a higher DHS rule amount, later CPI increments rounded down to$10 and Treasury disposition. It does not print the House one-viable-parent fee predicate or the House express waiver bar; no waiver availability or separate cumulative charges on every named payer are inferred. Complete1101(a)(27)(J) retains the juvenile-court dependency/custody and1ORboth-parent nonviability findings, best-interest-against-return finding, DHSconsent, HHS-specific custody-jurisdiction consent and no derivative parentage rights. These fee provisions do not grant SIJstatus, import a UAC-under18 definition or alter those eligibility findings by themselves. Senate100006 edits EXISTING1254a(c)(1)(B) registration authority: it raises the statutory fee MAXIMUM from$50 to$500, subject to fiscal2026-onward CPI-U adjustments rounded down to$10. It leaves the existing AttorneyGeneral MAYrequire a REASONABLE registration fee language and separate work-document fee authority; this is not a mandatory universal$500charge, a$500minimum, the House conditional additional fee or the separate$550initial/$275renewal EADfees. The amendment adds Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction of required fees. The existing appropriation-credit sentence is NOTEXPRESSLYSTRUCK in the printed edit and remains in redesignatedclause(i), alongside addedclause(iii) directing all fees under the subparagraph to Treasury. Preserve that apparent proceeds interaction for legal/application review rather than silently deleting the baseline sentence or choosing an implemented distribution. The proposed registration-cap change does not grant or end TPS, guarantee status eligibility, prove payment or establish an individual's outcome. Senate 100007 adds a visa-integrity fee payable by any alien issued a nonimmigrant visa at issuance, in addition to other authorized fees. The fiscal 2025 minimum is $250 or a higher DHS rule amount; subsequent July-to-July CPI-U increments are rounded down to the nearest dollar. Unreimbursed fees go to Treasury and the applicable fee cannot be waived or reduced. DHS MAY reimburse after the visa period of validity expires only if the alien demonstrates compliance with ALL visa conditions after admission, including no unauthorized employment, AND one of two printed alternatives: (A) did not seek to extend the period of admission during the visa validity period AND departed no later than five days after the last day of "such period"; OR (B) during that validity period WAS GRANTED an extension of nonimmigrant status or adjustment to lawful permanent resident status. The text uses "such period" in alternative (A); its application is reserved rather than silently choosing visa validity or authorized admission as the referent. The House nonuse, filing-only and change-of-status alternatives are not imported into this version. A filing is not a grant; reimbursement remains discretionary and conditional, not guaranteed repayment or a general permission to stay/work. The complete pre-vote 1101(a)(26) definition distinguishes proper nonimmigrant visa issuance from actual admission, compliance or an individual outcome. Senate 100008 separately adds an I-94 application fee on any alien submitting that application, with fiscal 2025 minimum $24 or higher DHS rule amount, later July-to-July CPI-U increments rounded down to the nearest dollar and no waiver/reduction. Twenty percent of collected fees goes to the existing Land Border Inspection Fee Account pursuant to 1356(q)(2), available to CBP to retain and spend without further appropriation for I-94 processing; amounts not deposited there go to Treasury. The complete pre-vote subsection (q) establishes the account and its land-port receipt/expense/report framework. That baseline account scope is not substituted for the new section's any-alien I-94 application predicate, and its appropriations refunds are not applicant reimbursements. The visa fee and I-94 fee have separate collection events and dispositions; neither proves actual admission, visa compliance, a collection or immigration-status outcome. Senate 100014 amends the existing ESTA fee components under complete pre-vote1187(h)(3): the existing $17 per travel authorization remains, the separate full-System-cost-recovery component gains a $10 MINIMUM while retaining that cost condition, and a new component is at least $13 PER TRAVEL AUTHORIZATION. This does not describe a $10 or $13 total or first creation of ESTA. Its sunset edit extends the clause(i)(I) Travel Promotion Fund fee restriction from fiscal years beginning after October31,2028 to those beginning after October31,2034; it is not a sunset of every component. Its fiscal2026-onward CPI-U adjustment names the clause(i)(II) amount but literally uses the prior fee required UNDER THIS SUBPARAGRAPH as its base. That component/base relationship remains a separate application question, not a silently substituted isolated cost component or definite whole-fee adjustment; no increment-rounding rule is printed. Unlike selected House70017, this section does not edit existing clause(ii) disposition language: that baseline directs (i)(I) to the Travel Promotion Fund and (i)(II) to Treasury for System administration, but does not assign newly added (i)(III) by name. The new $13 component's disposition is separately reserved, without copying the House Treasury sentence or claiming to have closed other package funding provisions. Exact officialPDFpages819-821 visually confirm the printed adjustment language and section boundary; no HTML-parser repair is made. Existing travel-eligibility/admissibility/visa-eligibility distinctions remain, and no express new ESTA fee-waiver prohibition or inferred waiver availability is imported from EVUS. Senate 100015 separately adds an EVUS fee at enrollment for any alien SUBJECT to that System, additional to other authorized fees, with fiscal2025 minimum $30 or a higher DHS rule amount, later CPI-U increments rounded down to $0.25 and no waiver/reduction. It inserts a new1356(w) CBP EVUS Account with deposits equal to fees received MINUS $5 multiplied by the NUMBER OF PAYMENTS collected; that same $5-times-payments amount goes to Treasury. This payment-count language is retained rather than substituted with House70019's per-enrollment wording or inferred one-payment-per-enrollment implementation. Account amounts are appropriated without further appropriation and available until expended for CBP EVUS administration costs. OfficialPDF823 confirms the payment-count basis. The fee does not expand who is subject to EVUS, establish admission or visa/status eligibility, prove compliance or document an actual payment. Senate 100013 adds ten EOIR fee provisions despite its narrower adjustment-of-status section title. In(a), an alien who files the specified adjustment application with immigration court OR whose application is adjudicated there pays at filing OR before court adjudication. In(b)/(c), the fee is required from any alien at court filing of the inadmissibility-waiver/TPS application OR before court adjudication. No automatic duplicate charge at both events is asserted. The(d)/(e) alien appeals, (f) practitioner appeal and(g) alien motion collect at filing. The(h) suspension application and(i) application for an alien who is a lawful permanent resident collect at court filing. Senate(j) separately requires a payer who IS NOT A LAWFUL PERMANENT RESIDENT at the time that payer files with immigration court a cancellation/adjustment application FOR ANY ALIEN; this wording is not silently collapsed into House's application-category wording or an assumed identity of payer and beneficiary. The ten listed fiscal2025 floors are separate fee events, additional to other authorized fees, with a higher AttorneyGeneral rule amount permitted: adjustment to lawful permanent residence $1,500; waiver of grounds of inadmissibility $1,050; TPS $500; appeal from an immigration-judge decision $900; appeal from a DHS-officer decision $900; practitioner disciplinary appeal $1,325; motion to reopen or reconsider an immigration-judge or Board of Immigration Appeals decision $900; suspension of deportation application $600; cancellation of removal for the specified permanent-resident category $600; and cancellation/adjustment for the specified nonpermanent-resident category $1,500. Each subsection has fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U adjustment of its own prior-year fee, with the INCREMENT rounded down to $10, not an automatically exact future price or a sum charged to every alien. The disciplinary appeal payer is a PRACTITIONER filing an appeal of an adjudicating official's decision in a practitioner disciplinary case, not every alien or every attorney. The immigration-judge appeal provision separately excludes appeals of BOND decisions. The motion-fee exception identifies only motions to REOPEN an IN-ABSENTIA removal order under240(b)(5)(C)(ii) or an in-absentia deportation order under legacy242B(c)(3)(B), with the version's own printed temporal wording retained below. Complete pre-vote1229a(b)(5)(C)(ii) allows the identified motion at any time upon demonstrating either lack of notice in accordance with1229(a)(1) OR(a)(2), OR Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault of the alien. Complete historical1252b(c)(3)(B) likewise allows the identified motion at any time upon demonstrating lack of notice in accordance with its(a)(2), OR Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault of the alien. The surrounding notice/address requirements remain; these are not exemptions for every missed hearing, any custody, all reopening/reconsideration motions, or the separate180-day exceptional-circumstances grounds in240(b)(5)(C)(i)/242B(c)(3)(A). A fee exception does not establish that a motion was granted or an order actually rescinded. The1995Code historical section is corroborated by the later repeal/history notice and enacted104-208: its intervening371(b)(7) changes only242B(d)(1) officer terminology, not(c)(3)(B), and its309 effective-date/transition provisions remain qualified. Current repeal metadata is not substituted for operative legacy text. Senate(g)(3)(B) literally ends with a motion filed in accordance with242B(c)(3)(B) PRIOR TO APRIL1,1997, without House's explicit AS THE SECTION EXISTED phrase. The printed date attachment remains an application question: no definite pre1997 filing cutoff or deletion of the date is accepted, and the underlying legacy statute's at-any-time text remains visible. OfficialPDF812 visually confirms the same wording; it is not repaired as a parser error. Senate100013 prints NO express section-wide no-waiver/reduction clause; House(k) is not imported and availability of a waiver is not inferred. Every(a)-(j) disposition instead names fees collected pursuant to THIS SUBSECTION, with a not-more-than25percent ExaminationsFeeAccount transfer/EOIR retention-and-spending cap and amounts not transferred/credited toTreasury; Senate(a) does not copy House's50percent cap. These ceilings are not mandatory actual percentages, direct refunds to applicants or new account creation. Senate(k) bars EOIR expenditure of section-collected fees for the Legal Orientation Program OR any successor, without establishing termination or a universal funding ban. No component preference follows from either member's whole-package vote. Senate 10108 replaces SNAP2015(f) with its own exact individual-status list. The replacement is a NECESSARY individual-status condition for a member of an OTHERWISE ELIGIBLE household, not a sufficient promise of SNAP entitlement. US RESIDENCE is common to EACH of the four alternatives, AND the individual must meet at least one listed category: (A) a citizen OR NATIONAL of the UNITED STATES; (B) the defined lawful permanent-resident immigrant, retaining the express exclusion of ordinary temporary visitors/tourists/diplomats/students with no intention of abandoning foreign residence; (C) the version's own status category described below; OR (D) an individual lawfully residing in the US IN ACCORDANCE WITH a Compact of Free Association referred to in PRWORA402(b)(2)(G). Complete1101(a)(15)/(20)/(22) defines immigrant/nonimmigrant classes, unchanged lawful permanent residence and US national, without treating every lawful temporary stay or every foreign national as a listed status. Complete1612(b)(2)(G) identifies the US Compacts with the Federated States of Micronesia, Marshall Islands and Palau; nationality alone is not substituted for the proposal's lawful-residence-under-Compact condition. The complete pre-vote2015(f) already requires residence and lists citizen/LPR, the specified1259 deemed-permanent-residence category, conditional entry under1157/1158, the described1182(d)(5) parole and withholding under1231(b)(3). (2) Eligible student.--The term `eligible student' means an individual who-- (A) is a member of a household with an income which, for the calendar year prior to the date of the application for a scholarship, is not greater than 300 percent of the area median gross income (as such term is used in section 42), and (B) is eligible to enroll in a public elementary or secondary school. ESTA has separate existing $17, full-cost-recovery-with-new-$10-minimum and new-at-least-$13 components. The extended sunset concerns only clause(i)(I). House70018 retains commercial-aircraft/vessel passenger inspection or preinspection events. One exception requires BOTH transit to an outside-US destination and no immigration inspection. A separate exception covers immigration inspection AT DESIGNATED PORTS OF ENTRY for BOTH following arrival types: (a) a ferry meeting the retained non-ocean/non-coastwise, only-deck-passenger-and/or-vehicle, short frequent direct-route and public bridge/tunnel-service definition; or (b) Great Lakes vessels on the Great Lakes and connecting waterways WHEN OPERATING ON A REGULAR SCHEDULE. EVUS fees apply at enrollment only to aliens subject to EVUS; neither a fee nor payment expands System eligibility or grants admission/status. EOIR100013 has TEN distinct fee events and fiscal2025 minimum/higher-rule amounts, each own annual CPI increment rounded DOWN to$10. The bond-appeal exception and the narrow IN-ABSENTIA REOPENING motions remain separate: upon DEMONSTRATION of (lack of the specifically required notice) OR (Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault), not any custody/missed hearing or all motions/reconsideration/180-day exceptional-circumstances claims. No fee or exception grants relief or rescinds an order. Senate(j) keeps a NON-LPR payer at court filing of a cancellation/adjustment application FOR ANY ALIEN. The Legal Orientation Program OR successor restriction concerns the identified section fees expended BY EOIR, not a demonstrated termination or every funding source.

SNAP10108 requires BOTH US RESIDENCE (common to EACH alternative) AND at least ONE own listed status: UScitizen OR USnational; definedLPR; version-specific(C); OR lawful USresidence INACCORDANCEWITH a referencedCOFA. An OTHERWISE ELIGIBLE household remains required; listed status alone does not grant benefits. Senate(C) retains HASBEENGRANTED definedCuban/Haitian-entrant status.
