claim_source_map.passage: 20303. Regional children's advocacy centers (a) Establishment and maintenance of regional children's advocacy program The Administrator shall establish and maintain a children's advocacy program to— (1) focus attention on child victims by assisting communities in developing child-focused, community-oriented, facility-based programs designed to improve the resources available to children and families; (2) enhance coordination among community agencies and professionals involved in the intervention, prevention, prosecution, and investigation systems that respond to child abuse cases; (3) train physicians and other health care and mental health care professionals, law enforcement officers, child protective service workers, forensic interviewers, prosecutors, victim advocates, multidisciplinary team leadership, and children's advocacy center staff, in the multidisciplinary approach to child abuse so that trained personnel will be available to provide support to community agencies and professionals involved in the intervention, prevention, prosecution, and investigation systems that respond to child abuse cases; (4) provide technical assistance, training, coordination, and organizational capacity support for State chapters; and (5) collaborate with State chapters to provide training, technical assistance, coordination, organizational capacity support, and oversight of— (A) local children's advocacy centers; and (B) communities that want to develop local children's advocacy centers. (b) Activities of regional children's advocacy program (1) Administrator The Administrator shall— (A) establish and maintain regional children's advocacy program centers; and (B) fund existing regional centers with expertise in multidisciplinary team investigation, trauma-informed interventions, and evidence-informed treatment, for the purpose of enabling grant recipients to provide information, services, training and technical assistance to aid communities in establishing and maintaining multidisciplinary programs that respond to child abuse. (2) Grant recipients A grant recipient under this section shall— (A) assist communities, local children's advocacy centers, multidisciplinary teams, and State chapters— (i) in developing and expanding a comprehensive, multidisciplinary response to child abuse that is designed to meet the needs of child victims and their families; (ii) in promoting the effective delivery of the evidence-informed Children's Advocacy Center Model and the multidisciplinary response to child abuse, including best practices in— (I) organizational support and development; (II) programmatic evaluation; and (III) financial oversight of Federal funding; (iii) in establishing child-friendly facilities for the investigation and intervention in child abuse; (iv) in preventing or reducing trauma to children caused by duplicative contacts with community professionals; (v) in providing families with needed services and assisting them in regaining maximum functioning; (vi) in maintaining open communication and case coordination among community professionals and agencies involved in child protection efforts; (vii) in coordinating and tracking investigative, preventive, prosecutorial, and treatment efforts; (viii) in obtaining information useful for criminal and civil proceedings; (ix) in holding offenders accountable through improved prosecution of child abuse cases; (x) in enhancing professional skills necessary to effectively respond to cases of child abuse through training; and (xi) in enhancing community understanding of child abuse; and (B) provide training and technical assistance to local children's advocacy centers, interested communities, and chapters in its census region that are grant recipients under section 20304 of this title. (c) Operation of regional children's advocacy program (1) Solicitation of proposals Not later than 1 year after November 4, 1992, the Administrator shall solicit proposals for assistance under this section. (2) Minimum qualifications In order for a proposal to be selected, the Administrator may require an applicant to have in existence, at the time the proposal is submitted, 1 or more of the following: (A) A proven record in conducting activities of the kinds described in subsection (c). (B) A facility where children who are victims of sexual or physical abuse and their nonoffending family members can go for the purpose of investigation and intervention in child abuse. (C) Multidisciplinary staff experienced in providing evidence-informed services for children and families. (D) Experience in serving as a center for training and education and as a resource facility. (E) National expertise in providing technical assistance to communities with respect to the multidisciplinary response to child abuse. (3) Proposal requirements (A) In general A proposal submitted in response to the solicitation under paragraph (1) shall— (i) include a single or multiyear management plan that outlines how the applicant will provide information, services, and technical assistance to communities and chapters so that communities can establish and maintain multidisciplinary programs that respond to child abuse and chapters can establish and maintain children's advocacy centers in their State; (ii) demonstrate the ability of the applicant to operate successfully a children's advocacy center or provide training to allow others to do so; and (iii) state the annual cost of the proposal and a breakdown of those costs. (B) Content of management plan A management plan described in paragraph (3)(A) shall— (i) outline the basic activities expected to be performed; (ii) describe the entities that will conduct the basic activities; (iii) establish the period of time over which the basic activities will take place; and (iv) define the overall program management and direction by— (I) identifying managerial, organizational, and administrative procedures and responsibilities; (II) demonstrating how implementation and monitoring of the progress of the children's advocacy program after receipt of funding will be achieved; and (III) providing sufficient rationale to support the costs of the plan. (4) Selection of proposals (A) Competitive basis Proposals shall be selected under this section on a competitive basis. (B) Criteria The Administrator shall select proposals for funding that— (i) best result in developing and establishing multidisciplinary programs that respond to child abuse by assisting, training, and teaching community agencies and professionals called upon to respond to child abuse cases; (ii) assist in resolving problems that may occur during the development, operation, and implementation of a multidisciplinary program that responds to child abuse; (iii) to the greatest extent possible and subject to available appropriations, ensure that at least 1 applicant is selected from each of the 4 census regions of the country; (iv) best result in supporting chapters in each State; and (v) otherwise best carry out the purposes of this section. (5) Funding of program From amounts made available in separate appropriation Acts, the Administrator shall provide to each grant recipient the financial and technical assistance and other incentives that are necessary and appropriate to carry out this section. (6) Coordination of effort In order to carry out activities that are in the best interests of abused and neglected children, a grant recipient shall consult with other grant recipients under this Act on a regular basis to exchange ideas, share information, and review children's advocacy program activities. (d) Review (1) Evaluation of regional children's advocacy program activities The Administrator shall regularly monitor and evaluate the activities of grant recipients and shall determine whether each grant recipient has complied with the original proposal and any modifications. (2) Annual report A grant recipient shall provide an annual report to the Administrator that— (A) describes the progress made in satisfying the purpose of the children's advocacy program; and (B) states whether changes are needed and are being made to carry out the purpose of the children's advocacy program. (3) Discontinuation of funding Upon discontinuation of funding of a grant recipient under this section, the Administrator shall solicit new proposals in accordance with subsection (c). (Pub. DIVISION G--DEPARTMENTS <<NOTE: Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2015. Department of Labor Appropriations Act, 2015.>> OF LABOR, HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, AND EDUCATION, AND RELATED AGENCIES APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2015 

Sec. 506. (a) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for any abortion. (b) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of abortion. (c) The term ``health benefits coverage'' means the package of services covered by a managed care provider or organization pursuant to a contract or other arrangement. Sec. 507. (a) The limitations established in the preceding section shall not apply to an abortion-- (1) if the pregnancy is the result of an act of rape or incest; or (2) in the case where a woman suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness, including a life-endangering physical condition caused by or arising from the pregnancy itself, that would, as certified by a physician, place the woman in danger of death unless an abortion is performed. (b) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as prohibiting the expenditure by a State, locality, entity, or private person of State, local, or private funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (c) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as restricting the ability of any managed care provider from offering abortion coverage or the ability of a State or locality to contract separately with such a provider for such coverage with State funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (d)(1) None of the funds made available in this Act may be made available to a Federal agency or program, or to a State or local government, if such agency, program, or government subjects any institutional or individual health care entity to discrimination on the basis that the health care entity does not provide, pay for, provide coverage of, or refer for abortions. (2) In this subsection, the term ``health care entity'' includes an individual physician or other health care professional, a hospital, a provider-sponsored organization, a health maintenance organization, a health insurance plan, or any other kind of health care facility, organization, or plan.

SEC. 4002. PREVENTION <<NOTE: 42 USC 300u-11.>> AND PUBLIC HEALTH FUND. (a) Purpose.--It is the purpose of this section to establish a Prevention and Public Health Fund (referred to in this section as the ``Fund''), to be administered through the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Secretary, to provide for expanded and sustained national investment in prevention and public health programs to improve health and help restrain the rate of growth in private and public sector health care costs. (b) Funding.--There are hereby authorized to be appropriated, and appropriated, to the Fund, out of any monies in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated-- (1) for fiscal year 2010, $500,000,000; (2) for fiscal year 2011, $750,000,000; (3) for fiscal year 2012, $1,000,000,000; (4) for fiscal year 2013, $1,250,000,000; (5) for fiscal year 2014, $1,500,000,000; and (6) for fiscal year 2015, and each fiscal year thereafter, $2,000,000,000. (c) Use of Fund.--The Secretary shall transfer amounts in the Fund to accounts within the Department of Health and Human Services to increase funding, over the fiscal year 2008 level, for programs authorized by the Public Health Service Act, for prevention, wellness, and public health activities including prevention research and health screenings, such as the Community Transformation grant program, the Education and Outreach Campaign for Preventive Benefits, and immunization programs. (d) Transfer Authority.--The Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives may provide for the transfer of funds in the Fund to eligible activities under this section, subject to subsection (c). 

(b) Section 4002(c) of this Act <<NOTE: 42 USC 300u-11.>> is amended-- [[Page 124 STAT. 975]] (1) by striking ``research and health screenings'' and inserting ``research, health screenings, and initiatives''; and (2) by striking ``for Preventive'' and inserting ``Regarding Preventive''.

Prevention and Public Health Fund (a) Purpose It is the purpose of this section to establish a Prevention and Public Health Fund (referred to in this section as the "Fund"), to be administered through the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Secretary, to provide for expanded and sustained national investment in prevention and public health programs to improve health and help restrain the rate of growth in private and public sector health care costs. (b) Funding There are hereby authorized to be appropriated, and appropriated, to the Fund, out of any monies in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated— (1) for fiscal year 2010, $500,000,000; (2) for each of fiscal years 2012 through 2017, $1,000,000,000; (3) for fiscal year 2018, $900,000,000; (4) for fiscal year 2019, $900,000,000; (5) for each of fiscal years 2020 and 2021, $950,000,000; (6) for each of fiscal years 2022 and 2023, $1,000,000,000; (7) for each of fiscal years 2024 and 2025, $1,300,000,000; (8) for each of fiscal years 2026 and 2027, $1,525,000,000; (9) for each of fiscal years 2028 and 2029, $1,725,000,000; and (10) for fiscal year 2030 and each fiscal year thereafter, $2,000,000,000. (c) Use of Fund The Secretary shall transfer amounts in the Fund to accounts within the Department of Health and Human Services to increase funding, over the fiscal year 2008 level, for programs authorized by the Public Health Service Act [42 U.S.C. 201 et seq.], for prevention, wellness, and public health activities including prevention research, health screenings, and initiatives, such as the Community Transformation grant program, the Education and Outreach Campaign Regarding Preventive Benefits, and immunization programs. (d) Transfer authority The Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives may provide for the transfer of funds in the Fund to eligible activities under this section, subject to subsection (c). United States Code, 2024 Edition Title 22 - FOREIGN RELATIONS AND INTERCOURSE CHAPTER 36 - MIGRATION AND REFUGEE ASSISTANCE Sec. 2601 - Refugees and migration From the U.S. Government Publishing Office, www.gpo.gov §2601. Refugees and migration (a) United States membership in International Organization for Migration; contributions to Organization (1) The President is authorized to continue membership for the United States in the International Organization for Migration in accordance with the constitution of such organization approved in Venice, Italy, on October 19, 1953, as amended in Geneva, Switzerland, on November 24, 1998, upon entry into force of such amendments. (2) For the purpose of assisting in the movement of refugees and migrants, there are authorized to be appropriated to the President such amounts as may be necessary from time to time for payment by the United States of its contributions to the International Organization for Migration and all necessary salaries and expenses incidental to United States participation in such organization. (b) Appropriations for assistance to refugees There are authorized to be appropriated such amounts as may be necessary from time to time— (1) for contributions to the activities of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees for assistance to refugees under his mandate or persons on behalf of whom he is exercising his good offices, and for contributions to the International Organization for Migration, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and to other relevant international organizations; and (2) for assistance to or on behalf of refugees who are outside the United States designated by the President (by class, group, or designation of their respective countries of origin or areas of residence) when the President determines that such assistance will contribute to the foreign policy interests of the United States. (c) United States Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund; appropriations (1) Whenever the President determines it to be important to the national interest he is authorized to furnish on such terms and conditions as he may determine assistance under this chapter for the purpose of meeting unexpected urgent refugee and migration needs. (2) There is established a United States Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund to carry out the purposes of this section. There is authorized to be appropriated to the President from time to time such amounts as may be necessary for the fund to carry out the purposes of this section, except that no amount of funds may be appropriated which, when added to amounts previously appropriated but not yet obligated, would cause such amounts to exceed $100,000,000. Amounts appropriated hereunder shall remain available until expended. (3) Whenever the President requests appropriations pursuant to this authorization he shall justify such requests to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, as well as to the Committees on Appropriations. (d) Information to Congressional committees The President shall keep the appropriate committees of Congress currently informed of the use of funds and the exercise of functions authorized in this chapter. (e) Continued availability of certain funds Unexpended balances of funds made available under authority of the Mutual Security Act of 1954, as amended, and of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as amended, [22 U.S.C. 2151 et seq.], and allocated or transferred for the purposes of sections 405(a), 405(c), 405(d) and 451(c) 1 of the Mutual Security Act of 1954, as amended [22 U.S.C. 1925(a), (c), (d), 1951(c)], are authorized to be continued available for the purposes of this section and may be consolidated with appropriations authorized by this section. (f) Restrictions on foreign assistance not applicable to migration and refugee assistance The President may furnish assistance and make contributions under this chapter notwithstanding any provision of law which restricts assistance to foreign countries. Appropriations for State Department; information to congressional committees (a)(1) Notwithstanding any provision of law enacted before October 26, 1974, no money appropriated to the Department of State under any law shall be available for obligation or expenditure with respect to any fiscal year commencing on or after July 1, 1972— (A) unless the appropriation thereof has been authorized by law enacted on or after February 7, 1972; or (B) in excess of an amount prescribed by law enacted on or after such date. (2) To the extent that legislation enacted after the making of an appropriation to the Department of State authorizes the obligation or expenditure thereof the limitation contained in paragraph (1) shall have no effect. (3) The provisions of this section— (A) shall not be superseded except by a provision of law enacted after February 7, 1972, which specifically repeals, modifies, or supersedes the provisions of this section; and (B) shall not apply to, or affect in any manner, permanent appropriations, trust funds, and other similar accounts administered by the Department as authorized by law. (b) The Department of State shall keep the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives fully and currently informed with respect to all activities and responsibilities within the jurisdiction of these committees. Any Federal department, agency, or independent establishment shall furnish any information requested by either such committee relating to any such activity or responsibility. United States Code, 2024 Edition Title 50 - WAR AND NATIONAL DEFENSE CHAPTER 44 - NATIONAL SECURITY SUBCHAPTER III - ACCOUNTABILITY FOR INTELLIGENCE ACTIVITIES Sec. 3094 - Funding of intelligence activities From the U.S. Government Publishing Office, www.gpo.gov §3094. Funding of intelligence activities (a) Obligations and expenditures for intelligence or intelligence-related activity; prerequisites Appropriated funds available to an intelligence agency may be obligated or expended for an intelligence or intelligence-related activity only if— (1) those funds were specifically authorized by Congress for use for such intelligence or intelligence-related activities; or (2) in the case of funds from the Reserve for Contingencies of the Central Intelligence Agency and consistent with the provisions of section 3093 of this title concerning any significant anticipated intelligence activity, the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency has notified the appropriate congressional committees of the intent to make such funds available for such activity; or (3) in the case of funds specifically authorized by the Congress for a different activity— (A) the activity to be funded is a higher priority intelligence or intelligence-related activity; (B) the use of such funds for such activity supports an emergent need, improves program effectiveness, or increases efficiency; and (C) the Director of National Intelligence, the Secretary of Defense, or the Attorney General, as appropriate, has notified the appropriate congressional committees of the intent to make such funds available for such activity; (4) nothing in this subsection prohibits obligation or expenditure of funds available to an intelligence agency in accordance with sections 1535 and 1536 of title 31. (b) Activities denied funding by Congress Funds available to an intelligence agency may not be made available for any intelligence or intelligence-related activity for which funds were denied by the Congress. (c) Presidential finding required for expenditure of funds on covert action No funds appropriated for, or otherwise available to, any department, agency, or entity of the United States Government may be expended, or may be directed to be expended, for any covert action, as defined in section 3093(e) of this title, unless and until a Presidential finding required by subsection (a) of section 3093 of this title has been signed or otherwise issued in accordance with that subsection. (d) Report to congressional committees required for expenditure of nonappropriated funds for intelligence activity (1) Except as otherwise specifically provided by law, funds available to an intelligence agency that are not appropriated funds may be obligated or expended for an intelligence or intelligence-related activity only if those funds are used for activities reported to the appropriate congressional committees pursuant to procedures which identify— (A) the types of activities for which nonappropriated funds may be expended; and (B) the circumstances under which an activity must be reported as a significant anticipated intelligence activity before such funds can be expended. (2) Procedures for purposes of paragraph (1) shall be jointly agreed upon by the congressional intelligence committees and, as appropriate, the Director of National Intelligence or the Secretary of Defense. (e) Definitions As used in this section— (1) the term "intelligence agency" means any department, agency, or other entity of the United States involved in intelligence or intelligence-related activities; (2) the term "appropriate congressional committees" means the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Select Committee on Intelligence and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and (3) the term "specifically authorized by the Congress" means that— (A) the activity and the amount of funds proposed to be used for that activity were identified in a formal budget request to the Congress, but funds shall be deemed to be specifically authorized for that activity only to the extent that the Congress both authorized the funds to be appropriated for that activity and appropriated the funds for that activity; or (B) although the funds were not formally requested, the Congress both specifically authorized the appropriation of the funds for the activity and appropriated the funds for the activity. house:119:1:145.mechanism: H.R.1 House reconciliation package: selected border, detention and asylum, employment-authorization and selected sponsor/enforcement fees
house:119:1:145.candidate_exact_action_meaning:
This May22 House passage is the whole H.R.1 reconciliation package, not a separate immigration-only vote. The controlling House choice uses H.Res.436: Rules Committee Print119-3 modified by the amendment printed in H.Rept.119-113 was considered adopted. The retained Immigration clauses are reconstructed against that chain and the contemporaneous as-amended floor Record. The currently served EH incorporates later corrections and renumbering and is a comparison witness for these unchanged selected clauses, not the controlling entire vote-time text. Later engrossment corrections and the July Senate replacement are not silently substituted for this choice. The description selects border infrastructure, detention, State reimbursement and asylum-fee mechanisms; it does not inventory every immigration-related tax, benefit, employment-authorization, child-sponsor or removal provision in this multi-domain package. Section60001 would make additional fiscal2025 CBP appropriations available until September30,2029: $46.5billion for primary/waterborne/secondary barriers, access roads and associated detection attributes; a separate $50million for specified invasive plants impeding RioGrande border operations; and $5billion for CBP facilities/checkpoints near the southwest, northern and maritime borders. These are different purposes, not one immigration-enforcement account or actual expenditures. The adopted manager amendment adds section60004: $12billion in additional fiscal2025 DHS funds, available until September30,2029, for grants reimbursing States for costs of actions on or after January21,2021 assisting federal border/immigration enforcement, including detention/removal and combating unlawful entry of persons/contraband. Applications need satisfactory cost evidence, and DHS cannot reimburse a State already reimbursed under another DHS grant program. This is funding subject to a process and conditions, not proof of State awards or a newly conferred State removal power. Section70101 would appropriate an additional $45billion for fiscal2025 to ICE, available until September30,2029, solely for single-adult alien detention and family residential-center capacity. DHS MAY detain family units pending a removal decision and, if ordered removed, until removal. Its family-center definition includes accompanied alien children, excludes unaccompanied alien children, and expressly applies regardless of State/local facility licensing. Its single-adult detention standards clause says they shall be set in the Secretary's SOLE discretion. Preserve that printed language without importing the Senate's express consistent-with-applicable-law qualification or deciding its interaction with judicial/other legal constraints. The existing unaccompanied-child definition in6USC279(g)(2) requires no lawful immigration status, age under18, and no US parent/legal guardian or none available for care/physical custody; childhood alone does not establish that category. Capacity funding and permission are not a universal detention mandate, removal order or actual detention outcome. Section70002 would require an additional fee at the time an alien files an asylum application: the fiscal2025 amount may be set by rule but cannot be less than $1,000. It cannot be waived/reduced. From fiscal2026 its amount increases using the prior fiscal-year fee and the printed July-to-July CPI-U increase, with the increment rounded down to a multiple of $10. Half of the Attorney-General-filed receipts go to EOIR; half of DHS-filed receipts go to USCIS's existing Immigration Examinations Fee Account; those credited amounts may be retained/spent without further appropriation, and the remainder goes to Treasury. Section70010 separately requires a fee for EACH CALENDAR YEAR an application remains pending, initially at least $100 for fiscal2025, with later CPI-U adjustment, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Its printed adjustment has no express rounding term; the filing-fee rounding rule is not copied into it. These are separate filing and pending-application charges, not fixed lifetime amounts or a claim that every asylum applicant actually paid. Section70023 changes existing INA208(d)(3)/8USC1158(d)(3) from MAY impose fees to SHALL, strikes the following cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory-fee language and preserves authority to set additional adjudication/naturalization fees under286(m). The existing paragraph already allowed fees for asylum consideration, employment authorization and asylum-based adjustment and capped them at adjudication costs; the bill does not create first-ever fee authority or establish a new substantive asylum eligibility test through that edit. Existing1356(m)/(n) supply the account/cost-recovery context. Employment-authorization provisions are separate from asylum filing and annual pending-application fees. House70003 would charge an additional fee on initial employment-authorization applications for asylum applicants underINA208(d)(2), paroled aliens and applicants underTPS244(a)(1)(B). Each initial fee has a fiscal2025 floor of$550, may be higher by DHS rule, cannot be waived/reduced and has the printed fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increment rounded down to$10. All three initial authorizations would last no more than six months. In70003(a)(4), the House allocation sentence says25percent of fees received UNDER THIS SECTION goes to USCIS's existing fee account to retain/spend without further appropriation, with50percent of that credited amount for benefit-fraud detection/prevention; uncredited amounts go to Treasury. The separately printed parole/TPS subsections direct their fees to Treasury. Preserve those exact scope words rather than silently deciding their interaction. House70012 and70014 separately impose additional parole/TPS employment-authorization renewal or extension fees with fiscal2025$550floors, possible higher rule amounts, subsequent CPI increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Both initial and renewed/extended authorizations in those sections last no more than six months. House70013 imposes at least$550 for each asylum-based renewal/extension, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction; that section prints no annual inflation formula. DHS MAY provide asylum-applicant employment authorization for at most six months, and each renewal/extension also has that limit. Authorization terminates immediately after an asylum-officer denial unless referred to an immigration judge;30days after an immigration-judge denial unless timely appealed to BIA; or immediately after BIA denies an appeal of asylum denial. After such termination DHS cannot grant, renew or extend it unless a FederalCourtOfAppeals remands to BIA. This restriction concerns employment authorization, not an automatic asylum denial, immediate removal or a bar on all judicial review. The pre-vote1158(d)(2) already says asylum applicants are not entitled to employment authorization but it may be provided by regulation; applicants not otherwise eligible cannot receive it before180days after asylum filing. Existing1254a(a)(1)(B)/(a)(2) authorizes employment and makes work authorization effective throughout TPS. Fee/document-validity provisions do not themselves end TPS, create first work authority or establish everyone's eligibility. The existing parole paragraph1182(d)(5)(A)/(B) is case-by-case urgent-humanitarian/significant-public-benefit authority subject to the printed statutory exceptions, including the refugee qualification and does not constitute admission. These fees do not supply a grant of parole or automatic employment permission. House70007 imposes a separate additional sponsor-placement fee, collected by HHS from the individual BEFORE placing an unaccompanied alien child underTVPRA235(c). Its fiscal2025 floor is$3,500 or a higher rule amount, with fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increments rounded down to$10 and no waiver/reduction. The stated purpose is partial reimbursement for the child's prior federal-custody processing, housing, food, education, transport and other care.25percent goes to HHS to retain/spend without further appropriation for sponsor/adult-household background checks; the remainder goes to Treasury. The specified checks include names, SSNs, dates of birth, validated residence, immigration status and contact information for the sponsor and all adult household residents, and records checks including sex-offender registry, public-records background and fingerprint-based national criminal history. Existing1232(c) already requires protective/suitability assessments, identity/relationship verification, independent risk findings and home studies in specified cases. This is not first-ever sponsor vetting or a new assertion that any sponsor has criminal activity. House70020 imposes ANOTHER additional sponsor fee BEFORE the unaccompanied child's release to the sponsor. The specialmixture/alternative-fuel claim needs BOTHatleast$200 ANDatleastoneweek; electronic claims disregard ONLYclause(i)'s amount threshold, retaining the oneweekminimum. Its deadline is the lastdayof the FIRSTquarter following the EARLIESTquarter included, unlike the ordinaryexception's LASTquarterbranch. Retain the printed45day/20dayelectronic payment/interest language and6621rate/method reference without resolving an actual accrual date or claim. Applicable-law/penalty/inconsistency rules and7602examination authority remain. The governmental/501exempt-person limitation has explicit exceptions for claims under(i)(2),(3),(4); do not turn it into a blanket private-producer bar. Section34and unread nested vendor/eligibility rules remain references, not completed programme classifications.

Other original4101controls remain bounded background: physical foreign-trade-zone/customs-bonded-terminal/refinery operation ORinventory-position registration, vessel-display and credit-card exempt-sale categories; reregistration after a transaction ORseries involving MORETHAN50percent ownership interests ORassets held by OTHERpersons compared with persons ORrelatedpersons who held MORETHAN50percent before, with the established-market-traded-corporation exception. This is not a foreign-influence threshold or universal ordinary-share-transfer rule. Discretionary bond ANDscoped lien, accepted substitute security/transfer/90dayresponse, denial-reference and information reporting/25ORMOREmonthlyelectronic requirements retain their own predicates and dated notes. No actual person/fuel/entity/territory/claim/registration/emissions/compliance/credit/codification/legal-priority classification, new Immigrationproposition or episode, reserved-question closure, full programme/package/domain/counterpart certificate, editorial acceptance or publication authority is supplied. All prior meaning, substantive legal questions, whole-package alternatives, member observations, withdrawals and denied/cancelled/closed-source restrictions remain.
house:119:1:145.candidate_short_description: H.R.1 House reconciliation package: selected border, detention and asylum, employment-authorization and selected sponsor/enforcement fees
house:119:1:145.candidate_compact_description: Selected House H.R. 1 provisions would fund border infrastructure and detention, set fiscal 2025 asylum filing/pending fee floors of $1,000/$100 and specified asylum/parole/TPS employment-authorization initial/renewal fee floors of $550, and limit those documents to at most six months. This is a whole-package passage choice, with qualifications.
candidate_shared_limitations: Selected source-bound Immigration highlights, not an exhaustive package or immigration-component inventory. The whole reconciliation measure also addresses taxes, benefits, defense, education, energy and other policies; a package vote cannot establish a separate position on any highlighted or omitted component.

House70101 prints a State-licensing-independent family-center definition and SOLE discretion over single-adult standards. It cannot be replaced by Senate90003's differently qualified text. Detention-law/judicial interactions require separate review; no universal custody duty, individual removal or legal enforceability ruling is inferred.

All listed appropriations are additional fiscal2025 amounts with September30,2029 availability. The State reimbursement provision requires costs associated with actions taken on or after January21,2021 and satisfactory evidence of costs incurred and bars specified duplicate DHS reimbursement. Availability is not actual spending, awards, detention or removal.

Asylum filing and yearly pending-application fees are separate additional charges with fiscal2025 floors, not guaranteed exact prices; the recurring trigger is each calendar year pending. Filing-fee CPI increments round down to $10; the House yearly-fee formula prints no rounding rule. Both have express no-waiver/reduction clauses.

The pre-vote INA fee paragraph already authorizes fees. Its MAY-to-SHALL edit and deletion of cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory language are distinguished from initial authority and substantive asylum eligibility. No later fee implementation rule or PublicLaw119-21 is imported as the pre-vote baseline.

H.Res.436/RCP119-3/adopted119-113 amendment control the May22 choice. June11H.Res.499/492 corrections and the July1EAS are separately recorded version events, not back-projected; the capturedEH is later corrected/renumbered and only the independently compared retained clauses are used here. The later Senate concurrence remains another question in this same episode without a trajectory claim.

Employment-authorization fees/durations concern specified initial or renewed/extended documents; they do not themselves confer work permission, end TPS or grant parole. Pre-vote1158(d)(2) no-entitlement/regulation/180day condition and1254a(a) continuingTPS work authority are retained. Whole-package observations do not establish support/opposition to any fee or duration component.

House initial and renewal/extension document limits are at most six months; Senate parole/TPS initial limits are one year or status duration, whichever shorter. Asylum-initial/renewal Senate sections do not print the House six-month sentence. Asylum-renewal House550/Senate275floors have no printed annual CPI rule; other listed EAD fees preserve their separate annual10dollar-rounded increments. Termination exceptions remain; only House prints the extra post-termination remand prohibition.

Printed EAD allocation/antecedent issues remain application questions: House70003(a)(4) uses UNDER THIS SECTION while parole/TPS fee clauses say Treasury; Senate100010 says renewal/extension OF SUCH PAROLE in its duration sentence. Preserve the source words, not a silently resolved interpretation.

Selected enforcement fees distinguish a prior in-absentia removal order PLUS later ICE arrest from an inadmissible person apprehended BETWEEN ports. Fiscal2025floors5000 may be higher by rule with separately printed CPI increments. Rescinded-order exception and notice/address/exceptional-circumstances/reopening-stay baseline remain. No new removal ground or actual order/arrest/collection follows from a package vote.

House sponsor fees are separate3500and5000fiscal2025floors collected BEFOREplacement/release, not only after a child misses court;5000reimbursement is discretionary/qualified, including a rescinded-order seek-reimbursement route. Existing placement/suitability protections are retained. These conditions and fees do not supply a new suitability finding, actual court default, automatic refund or removal outcome.

Parole-entry fees preserve all printed medical/family/transplant/adoption/temporary-return/hearing/law-enforcement predicates, not generic humanitarian labels. House Cuba-residence/family-visa/program conjunction differs from Senate granted-Cuban/Haitianentrant condition with its full definition. Exceptions and waiver bars are distinct; neither fee payment nor an exception creates parole/admission/status or an actual exemption.

HouseSIJ500minimum is conditional on its one-viable-parent/other-nonviable predicate; SenateSIJ250minimum namesalien/parent/legalguardian and lacks that House condition/expresswaiverbar. Existing complete1101(a)(27)(J), not(a)(15)(J), supplies court/best-interest/consent/parentage qualifications; no UACage rule, duplicate-payer charges or waiver availability inferred.

HouseTPS500additionalminimum has the exact non-admission/lapsed-nonimmigrant predicate. Senate raises existing50registrationMAXIMUMto500 and retainsreasonableMAY authority; do not substitute a universal500charge or copy the House floor/status scope. Its addedTreasury sentence coexists with an unstruck appropriation-credit baseline sentence, preserved as an application question. EADfees/status grant/duration and registration fee authority remain distinct.

Visa-integrity reimbursement is discretionary and available only after the visa period of validity expires. House requires demonstration of one of three alternatives: no admission sought during that validity period; or compliance with all visa conditions after admission, including no unauthorized employment, together with departure no later than five days after the date authorized to remain; or filing to extend, change or adjust status within visa validity. Senate requires post-admission compliance with all visa conditions in BOTH alternatives, including no unauthorized employment, together with either (A) no request to extend the period of admission during the visa validity period AND departure no later than five days after the last day of "such period", or (B) a GRANTED nonimmigrant extension or adjustment to lawful permanent resident status during the visa validity period. The printed Senate "such period" referent remains a separate application question. Filing is not a grant; visa validity is not admission duration; the five-day reimbursement conditions do not establish general stay/work permission.

I-94 fees attach to any-alien form application, not necessarily every entry or only land ports. The existing account deposit and appropriations refund do not create applicant refund rights. Preserve House lack of express CPI rounding versus Senate nearest-dollar increment rounding, 20-percent CBP account share and Treasury remainder separately from the visa fee.

ESTA has separate existing $17, full-cost-recovery-with-new-$10-minimum and new-at-least-$13 components. The extended sunset concerns only clause(i)(I). Both CPI amendments name clause(i)(II) but retain broader literal prior-base references; application is reserved, with no guessed fee total or increment-rounding rule. Selected House70017 edits dispositions; selected Senate100014 does not assign new(i)(III) by name. Do not transfer House account terms or EVUS waiver language into that Senate section; other package funding coverage remains partial.

House70018 retains commercial-aircraft/vessel passenger inspection or preinspection events. One exception requires BOTH transit to an outside-US destination and no immigration inspection. A separate exception covers immigration inspection AT DESIGNATED PORTS OF ENTRY for BOTH following arrival types: (a) a ferry meeting the retained non-ocean/non-coastwise, only-deck-passenger-and/or-vehicle, short frequent direct-route and public bridge/tunnel-service definition; or (b) Great Lakes vessels on the Great Lakes and connecting waterways WHEN OPERATING ON A REGULAR SCHEDULE. The designated-port condition applies in either arrival branch; each branch keeps its own definition/location/schedule conditions. Removing the geographical-origin exemption and replacing the separate $3 vessel charge are distinct edits. The new $1 Treasury sentence and unstruck all-(d)-receipts account baseline remain an application question, not a resolved distribution or applicant refund.

EVUS fees apply at enrollment only to aliens subject to EVUS; neither a fee nor payment expands System eligibility or grants admission/status. House deducts $5 per enrollment, while Senate deducts $5 times payments collected; do not equate those units silently. $30 is a fiscal2025 minimum/higher-rule boundary, CPI increments round down to$0.25, waiver bars apply to EVUS and account spending permission does not prove actual expenditure.

House70011 charges each continuance only when an alien BOTH requests it AND is granted it by an immigration judge. The separate NO-FEE exception requires a grant BASED ON statutory exceptional circumstances; it is not a waiver or any request/ordinary good cause. Circumstances must be beyond the alien's control and exclude less compelling circumstances. Examples remain illustrative: battery/extreme cruelty to the alien or the alien's child/parent; serious illness of the alien; or serious illness/death of the alien's spouse/child/parent. Each keeps its own person/event predicates; the examples are not an exclusive list. $100 is a fiscal2025 minimum or higher rule amount, not a guaranteed price; later CPI increments have no printed rounding rule.

House70015 separately charges diversity application at filing ($400minimum/higher rule) and program registration at registration ($250minimum/higher rule). Only the application CPI increment expressly rounds down to$10; both applicable fees have waiver/reduction bars. Two separate10percent shares concern SECTION receipts for the stated fraud/cost andICE purposes; unused/uncredited amounts goTreasury without proving cash distribution. Existing allocation rules remain, and eligibility requires EITHER high-school education/equivalent OR at least two years of work experience within five years of visa application in an occupation requiring at least two years of training/experience. Work alone is not that qualified-work branch. Registration/payment neither creates the program nor guarantees selection/visa.

EOIR70016 has TEN distinct fee events and fiscal2025 minimum/higher-rule amounts, each own annual CPI increment rounded DOWN to$10. Court application filing OR applicable prior adjudication is distinct from appeal/motion filing; no automatic double charge. Practitioner disciplinary appeals charge the filing PRACTITIONER. The bond-appeal exception and the narrow IN-ABSENTIA REOPENING motions remain separate: upon DEMONSTRATION of (lack of the specifically required notice) OR (Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault), not any custody/missed hearing or all motions/reconsideration/180-day exceptional-circumstances claims. No fee or exception grants relief or rescinds an order. House(g) expressly uses the legacy SECTION AS IT EXISTED beforeApril1,1997, not a filing cutoff; House(k) no-waiver/reduction remains distinct from nonapplication exceptions. Repeated SECTION-wide50percent(a)/25percent(b)-(j) account-transfer caps are reserved for application review, not silently converted to per-fee/fixed/cumulative shares. The Legal Orientation Program OR successor restriction concerns the identified section fees used to fund those programs, not a demonstrated termination or every funding source.

SNAP10012 requires BOTH US RESIDENCE (common to EACH alternative) AND at least ONE own listed status: UScitizen OR USnational; definedLPR; version-specific(C); OR lawful USresidence INACCORDANCEWITH a referencedCOFA. An OTHERWISE ELIGIBLE household remains required; listed status alone does not grant benefits. House(C) requires Cuban citizen/national AND ALL: APPROVED203(a)petition, ALLvisa eligibility with visa NOT immediately available, NOT otherwise inadmissible, AND PHYSICAL USpresence pursuant to the specified1994/1995commitment parole. No living-in-Cuba condition is printed in this SNAPclause; do not import the different parole-FEE exception or Senateentrant category. The rewritten(f) replaces its old list, not every separate public-benefit law or every person's full eligibility. Existing qualified-status/program restrictions/exceptions and2024COFA framework remain source-bound; no firstCOFA eligibility or blanket refugee/parolee outcome is claimed. The INELIGIBLE INDIVIDUAL'S income (less pro-rata share AT STATE OPTION) AND resources remain counted for that household's eligibility/allotment; the option concerns income subtraction, not automatic whole-household disqualification or all-resource exclusion.

House section 44110 begins October 1, 2026. Specified verification-period assistance becomes a STATE OPTION; federal payment for assistance during those periods is barred UNLESS the applicable status is VERIFIED BY THE END of the period. Election alone does not guarantee payment or individual eligibility. The first clerical-resolution effort still requires continued assistance WHILE MAKING THAT EFFORT. The separate 90-day process starts on INDIVIDUAL RECEIPT of notice; subsequent disenrollment/denial as applicable retains the printed OR predicate and 30 days AFTER the 90-day period. Other reasonable opportunities are not all 90 days. Medicaid-specific qualifiers do not rewrite every other 1137 program. Existing documentary exceptions, named emergency-treatment exclusions and appeal rights remain source-bound; lack of verification does not establish unlawful status or universal immediate loss of assistance. CHIP incorporates the payment restriction and State option. Neither clause supplies the other version's assistance/rate rule, resolves every individual benefit determination or closes the whole package; FMAP clauses are separate from this verification/status description.

House section 44111 quotes an expansion-rate change from 90 to 80 percent ONLY for a SPECIFIED STATE'S qualifying calendar quarters beginning October 1, 2027; it is not all Medicaid or every State's spending. The financial-assistance trigger retains BOTH exclusions (not qualified AND not a lawfully residing child/pregnant woman RECEIVING 1903(v)(4) assistance) for BOTH the assistance recipient/on-behalf-of alien AND the insurance-covered alien. The alternative is comprehensive coverage for an alien with both exclusions, regardless of source of funds or plan/program location. Defined insurance is not every health expense, and emergency care alone is not declared comprehensive coverage. The modified qualified-alien definition, printed parole carveout, coverage/assistance timing and State-opinion predicates remain. The (z)(2) formula has its own early-expansion cohort and quarter substitutions. The printed 1395d versus SSA section 1905 citation and shortened 1905(y)(C) anchors remain RESERVED; no repaired legal application or actual qualifying-State loss is accepted. This remains a qualified whole-package candidate component, without a component preference, individual award or full-package closure.

Medicare section 1899C requires ONE own listed category: US citizen OR US national; lawful permanent residence; version-specific category(3); OR lawful US residence under a referenced COFA. The new list has NO NEW COMMON RESIDENCE modifier across all alternatives. Separate existing entitlement/enrollment predicates remain; the existing five-year LPR residence rule retains its own enrollment path, not every citizen or insured-benefit path. Listed status alone is not sufficient. House category(3) requires Cuban nationality AND ALL approved 203(a)-petition, all-visa-eligibility-but-no-immediate-visa, no-other-inadmissibility and physical-US-presence-under-specified-parole predicates; no fee-derived living-in-Cuba condition. For those entitled/enrolled AS OF ENACTMENT, the restriction begins ONE YEAR AFTER ENACTMENT, with review completed within SIX MONTHS of enactment. EACH person identified as outside ALL four categories receives notice as soon as practicable AFTER IDENTIFICATION, designed for comprehension and naming the enactment-relative termination date. Review, notice and termination are distinct; the grace is not from notice, a guaranteed minimum notice period, every later applicant or perpetual grandfathering. No vote-date/later-law calendar substitution, actual review/termination, individual award or whole-package closure follows.

ACA status treatment concerns a LAWFULLY PRESENT ALIEN who IS AND IS REASONABLY EXPECTED FOR THE ENTIRE CREDIT-ENROLLMENT PERIOD to hold an own listed LPR, version-specific Cuban-related or COFA status; these conditions are common to each alternative. Citizens/US nationals retain the separate existing condition. Status alone does not satisfy all credit/program requirements. House prints IF AND ONLY IF and retains ALL Cuban nationality/petition/visa/inadmissibility/physical-parole predicates, without a fee-derived living-in-Cuba condition. Its named conforming provisions extend to credit AND reduced cost-sharing verification, individual cost-sharing/family rules and basic-health exclusions; the printed parenthetical is not repaired. Both credit restrictions retain the named section 151 tax-family condition (including taxpayer/spouse), INDIVIDUAL premium attribution and family-size/household-income calculations, not automatic whole-household loss or an insurance-enrollment ban. Both delete the special rule requiring ALL income NOT GREATER THAN 100 percent, lawful presence and Medicaid ineligibility BY REASON OF ALIEN STATUS. This does not alone prove credit loss at EXACTLY 100 percent, where the ordinary floor begins. The repeal starts taxable years after December 31, 2025; the status changes use taxable years after December 31, 2026 versus conforming PLAN YEARS on/after January 1, 2027. House additionally renumbers 36B(c)(1), removes the own basic-health special branch and cost-sharing reference sentence. The 5000A(d)(3) reference change does not amend the existing zero monetary penalty components. No actual award, revived penalty, whole-package closure or component preference follows.

Exchange verification concerns INDIVIDUAL CREDIT COVERAGE MONTHS, not an enrollment ban: failure of this paragraph ALONE does NOT make an individual ineligible to enroll. Applicant PROVIDED OR VERIFIED information applies TO THE EXTENT RELEVANT. House requires enrollment, advance credit AND reduced cost-sharing verification, names ANY immigration status, and prints IF AND ONLY IF for past-month verification FOR THAT MONTH. Its March 19, 2025 reference is the exact PROPOSED RULE full (f)(4), not June final/current CFR. House 44201(b)(1) requires ALL four discrepancy predicates, reliable data, the approved threshold of NOT LESS THAN 10 PERCENT (may ALSO be dollars), and no Medicaid/CHIP income-standard finding. Its exception is ONLY THIS DISCREPANCY SUBPARAGRAPH AND lawfully present alien AND Medicaid-ineligible BECAUSE OF ALIEN STATUS; not the separate missing-Treasury-data branch. Existing clerical/contact, documentary OR verifying-person resolution, 90 days WHEN NOTICE IS SENT, provisional determinations and appeals remain distinct. Other annual-filing/automatic-extension clauses remain separate. Both filing-compliance references retain HHS notification, advances for filer OR married spouse, the relevant tax-data year and failure to file/reconcile, with direct filer failure notice OR protected indirect risk/education notice; not a test imposed without those predicates or guaranteed notice-to-loss interval. ANY APPLICANT MAY use an Exchange-provided process BEGINNING NOT LATER THAN AUGUST 1 for the SUBSEQUENT PLAN YEAR; not a universal applicant deadline. House process covers enrollment, advance credit AND cost-sharing. Sections 112201/71303 apply to TAXABLE YEARS BEGINNING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2027, distinct from the House discrepancy PLAN YEARS ON/AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026 and the Senate incorporated-rule duration. No automatic credit/coverage outcome, whole-package closure or component preference is inferred.

House annual advance-credit determination retains prior ISSUER payment, RELEVANT TAX-DATA YEAR, Treasury-based Exchange determination, NOT FILED AS REQUIRED OR NOT RECONCILED AS NECESSARY; no universal return duty or actual tax debt. Attestation requires filing AND necessary reconciliation; Secretary MAY make an INITIAL determination AND MAY delay for a Secretary-determined REASONABLE PERIOD. Noncompliance determination AND notice to Exchange trigger exact PLAN YEAR 2025(i) protected notice alternatives; its printed second-year wording is not silently replaced by March/June rules or a guaranteed grace period. Removal concerns ONLY the AUTOMATIC 60-DAY HOUSEHOLD-INCOME-DOCUMENT EXTENSION: separate demonstrated-GOOD-FAITH extension and own clerical/interim/special-circumstance rules remain. 90 days starts when notice is SENT; the case-by-case documentary exception excludes citizenship/immigration-status inconsistencies. Own plan years begin on/after January 1, 2026. NO reduction for ANY MONTH UNLESS a COVERAGE MONTH FOR WHICH 36B CREDIT IS ALLOWED TO THE INSURED OR AN APPLICABLE TAXPAYER ON THE INSURED'S BEHALF: necessary, not sufficient, and not every insured personally filing. Definitions share 36B terms; data use ADVANCE-DETERMINATION TAX YEAR, not credit-allowed tax year. The undeleted cost-sharing sentence/basic-health branch alone does not establish continuing benefits. Question 34 remains RESERVED, without actual credit/reduction/basic-health award or loss, legal repair, full-package closure or acceptance.

House remittance tax is 3.5 percent. Its exception requires a written-agreement qualified provider and that provider must verify the sender as either a US citizen or a US national. The provider/agreement and verification conditions apply to both categories, rather than mere assertion, any provider or an SSN alone. Printed EFTA 920(g) versus 1693o-1/919 crosswalk stays RESERVED. New36C heading versus ANY INDIVIDUAL, taxpayer-paid tax, own/spouse qualified SSNs issued BEFORE RETURN DUE DATE, SIMILAR 32(d) rules, Secretary-satisfactory substantiation and literal 6050BB information reference stay qualified; no automatic citizen refund/noncitizen outcome. Reporting separates exempt aggregates, own certified-intent/name/tax records and other aggregates; not SSNs for every transfer. Credit uses TAXABLE YEARS ENDING AFTER December 31, 2025, not beginning. Both retain consumer/NATURAL-PERSON sender in a DEFINED STATE, provider-initiated ELECTRONIC transfer to FOREIGN designated recipient, account-independence, normal-course provider and SMALL-VALUE exclusion. Physical funding is distinct from electronic transfer technology. SENDER pays; provider COLLECTS FROM SENDER AND REMITS QUARTERLY; secondary liability ONLY unpaid-at-transfer AND uncollected extent. Transfers apply AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2025. Anti-conduit deeming/regulatory discretion is not observed avoidance, wrongdoing or an individual tax finding. No specific person, provider, transaction path, credit/refund or actual net-cost outcome is determined.

House 44201(i) applies to an ALIEN GRANTED DEFERRED ACTION under the named JUNE 15, 2012 process, not mere criteria/request/work authorization. Three printed scopes differ: IN THIS TITLE (1312), FOR PURPOSES OF THIS SECTION (1402), FOR PURPOSES OF THE PREVIOUS SENTENCE (1412 Federal payments/credits/reductions). Literal amendments MADE BY THIS SECTION apply WITH RESPECT TO PLAN YEARS BEGINNING ON OR AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026. Own individual-market Exchange/qualified-plan, silver-plan/income, whole-enrollment and individual/family boundaries and necessary allowed-credit/month dependency remain. Pre-vote State flexibility is not a guaranteed award or accepted workaround. Original memo requires background check AND CASE-BY-CASE determination, no assurance of relief, distinct encounter/pending-removal/non-removal paths and renewable two-year periods. AT LEAST 15 is not universal; final-order REGARDLESS OF THEIR AGE is preserved with question 38 reserved. Work authorization is APPLICATION TO DETERMINE WHETHER QUALIFIED, not automatic. Memo confers NO SUBSTANTIVE RIGHT, IMMIGRATION STATUS OR PATHWAY TO CITIZENSHIP; this does not independently determine ACA lawful presence. Original awkward criterion words, distinct original 60-day memo clock and actual Supreme Court/DOJ provenance are retained. No current eligibility/validity, current grant, motives, all-insurance ban, whole-household loss or individual benefit finding.

House requires TAXPAYER AND CHILD AND IF MARRIED SPOUSE SSNs; SIMILAR 32(d) includes its own separated-spouse reference, not automatic identity or universal separate-return denial. The temporary $2,500 substitution applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, and before December 31, 2028. The $2,000 substitution applies to any subsequent taxable year. The separate credit-amount inflation applies in a taxable year beginning after 2028. Separate 110003 after-2025 date retained. Both child-credit amendments begin with TAXABLE YEARS BEGINNING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2024. The defined SSN may be issued to either a US citizen or an individual under the named work-authorized-alien branch. In either case, it must have been issued before the due date for the return. Any SSA number, an ITIN or citizenship proof alone is insufficient. Complete 24/152 retain own qualifying-child, NOT-ATTAINED-17, citizenship/residence/adoption, relationship/support/abode/joint-return/tie/custody and other exceptions, income/refundable/identification/year limits. Existing 24(h)(4)(C) PARAGRAPH (7) fallback is RETAINED but new claimant/spouse-failure application RESERVED as question 39: no guaranteed $500 or whole-family loss. Zero-exemption reference rule does not itself eliminate credit. Mathematical-error scope changes to SECTION 24; own alleged-error/explanation notice, no petition BASED ON THAT NOTICE, abatement request WITHIN 60 DAYS AFTER NOTICE SENT, mandatory abatement UPON RECEIPT, deficiency reassessment and collection stay remain. No actual fraud, debt, indexed payment, credit/refund, every-remedy loss or individual/tax-family determination.

The House $4,000 bonus concerns aged section 63(f)(1), with its own age-65 and spouse/exemption conditions, rather than a blind-only bonus. The phaseout rate is 4 percent over $75,000, or $150,000 on a joint return. The taxpayer must supply the defined SSN; if married, the spouse's defined SSN is also required, with the separate similar-32(d) context. Printed new-paragraph inflation and hypothetical aggregate itemizer conditions remain qualified. Floor closing-quotation placement differs from later EH; question 40 reserves exact application, without silently repaired or guaranteed (E)/(F) outcomes. Own mathematical-error label is (Z). The same-version SSN definition permits issuance to either a US citizen or the named work-authorized-alien category. In either case, the number must have been issued before the due date for the return. Other SSA numbers or ITINs do not alone qualify. Child-credit identification is not senior identification. Own taxable-income, itemization, spouse/exemption and marital predicates remain, along with the nonresident-alien standard-deduction exclusion, without an individual eligibility finding or accepted override. A deduction is not a dollar-for-dollar credit, exemption of all Social Security income or guaranteed refund. Both senior amendments apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024; their own upper limit is a taxable year beginning before January 1, 2029. Modified income includes the named 911/931/933 exclusions. Mathematical-error notice requires the alleged error and explanation; the no-petition rule concerns that notice. The abatement request period is 60 days after notice is sent, abatement follows receipt, reassessment uses deficiency procedures and collection is stayed during the abatement period. No actual debt, fraud, payment or loss of every remedy.

House requires the taxpayer's defined SSN in all cases. A married individual must also include the spouse's defined SSN; a credit for the qualified expenses of an individual other than the taxpayer or spouse must also include that individual's name and defined SSN. Own similar-32(d) marital replacement retains distinct separated-spouse context without automatic identical application or universal separate-return denial. The same-version defined SSN permits citizen issuance or the named work-authorized-alien branch. In either case, issuance must precede the return due date; an ITIN or any SSA number does not alone suffice. The old AOTC student on-or-before deadline is distinct. The institution EIN clause is AOTC-only and tied to the named taxpayer-paid qualified expenses taken into account, with retained dependent-payment treatment; it is not a Lifetime Learning or every-institution requirement. Full credit, income, student, institution, qualified-expense, assistance, dependent, prepayment, double-benefit, payee-statement, refund and recapture conditions remain, without an individual amount or eligibility determination. The AOTC student reference freezes HEA 484(a)(1), with its own exceptions, at August 5, 1997; it does not import all current student eligibility or its citizenship paragraph. The institution definition retains frozen HEA 481 and its own title IV eligibility condition. Exact historical passages and amendment chronology are bound; full HEA 481 comparison uses two declared split-word normalizations, without source mutation or personal/institution classification. A taxpayer nonresident during any portion of the year retains the conditional 6013(g)/(h) chapter-1 resident-election path, each with own spouse/status/both-election and duration/termination/re-election predicates; this is not all-noncitizen denial or immigration status/work authorization. Both apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Own mathematical-error (J) changes TIN to SSN or EIN; alleged-error/explanation notice, 60 days after notice is sent, abatement upon receipt, deficiency reassessment and collection stay remain. No debt, wrongdoing, guaranteed credit/refund, loss of every remedy or whole-package closure.

House 30001 replaces only current HEA 484(a)(5): US citizen or national, INA lawful permanent resident, the five-condition Cuban alternative, or lawful US residence under a named COFA. Residence is not made common to every alternative. All five Cuban conditions must hold: Cuban citizen or national; approved INA 203(a) family-preference petition; all immigrant-visa eligibility but no immediately available visa; not otherwise inadmissible under 212(a); and physical US presence pursuant to the parole grant tied to the two named migration agreements. Nationality, any parole, visa or other Cuban/Haitian-entrant label alone is insufficient. Parole is not admission or a new grant of immigration status. Original September 1994 text and grant/programme matching are unfinished research, not evidence unavailability or an accepted classifier. Full current aid prerequisites and conditional student/programme exceptions remain. Immigration and SSN verification, reasonable-opportunity/pending and institution/loan-guarantee protections retain their printed predicates; question 41 reserves stale documentation cross-reference application, without repair or a promised interval. The intellectual-disability path expressly retains (a)(5) among its named prerequisites; own limited waiver is not a blanket award. The confined-Pell notwithstanding/otherwise-eligible/programme clause remains, with interaction reserved as question 42; no universal aid loss or guaranteed exception. Own incarcerated-loan restriction is not every-Pell denial. Effective July 1, 2025, for award year 2025-2026 and each subsequent award year, under the July 1-June 30 award-year definition. Academic and tax years are distinct. No actual grant, individual eligibility, scholarship-wide ban, enactment claim, Senate counterpart, frozen-tax-reference substitution or whole-package closure.

Selected exact House account and separate pilot eligibility clauses follow. House 110115 account establishment and instrument: The term `TRUMP account' means a trust created or organized in the United States for the exclusive benefit of an individual and which is designated (in such manner as the Secretary shall prescribe) at the time of the establishment of the trust as a TRUMP account, but only if the written governing instrument creating the trust meets the following requirements: (A) The individual establishing the account shall provide to the trustee the social security number of such individual and of the account beneficiary. (B) Except in the case of a qualified rollover contribution described in subsection (e), no contribution will be accepted-- (i) before January 1, 2026, (ii) unless it is in cash, (iii) unless the account beneficiary has not attained age 18, and (iv) if such contribution would result in aggregate contributions for the taxable year exceeding the contribution limit specified in subsection (c)(1). (C) No distribution (other than a distribution of a qualified rollover contribution) will be allowed-- (i) before the date on which the account beneficiary attains age 18, or (ii) in the case of such an account the account beneficiary of which has not attained age 25, if the aggregate distributions from such account exceeds the amount that is \1/2\ the cash equivalent value of the account on the date on which the account beneficiary attains age 18. (D) The account beneficiary has not attained age 8 on the date of the establishment of the account. (E) The trustee is a bank (as defined in section 408(n)) or another person who demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Secretary that the manner in which that person will administer the trust will be consistent with the requirements of this section or who has so demonstrated with respect to any individual retirement plan. (F) The interest of an individual in the balance of his account is nonforfeitable. (G) The assets of the trust shall not be commingled with other property except in a common trust fund or common investment fund. (H) No part of the trust funds will be invested in any asset other than eligible investments. House 110115 account beneficiary: The term `account beneficiary' means the individual on whose behalf the TRUMP account was established. House 110115 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. House 110116 one-time credit and account-only payment: In the case of any taxpayer with respect to whom an eligible individual is a qualifying child, there shall be allowed a one-time credit of $1,000 with respect to each such eligible individual who is a qualifying child of such taxpayer which shall be payable by the Secretary only to the TRUMP account with respect to which such eligible individual is the account beneficiary. House 110116 Secretary account establishment and opt-out: (1) In general.--In the case of any eligible individual that the Secretary determines is not the account beneficiary of any TRUMP account as of the qualifying date of such eligible individual, the Secretary shall establish an account for the benefit of such eligible individual. (2) Qualifying date.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `qualifying date' means, with respect to an eligible individual, the first date on which a return of tax is filed by an individual with respect to whom such eligible individual is a qualifying child with respect to the taxable year to which such return relates. (3) Notification.--In the case of any eligible individual for the benefit of whom the Secretary establishes an account under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall-- (A) notify any individual with respect to whom such eligible individual is a qualifying child for the taxable year described in paragraph (2) of the establishment of such account, and (B) shall provide an opportunity to such individual to elect to decline the application of this subsection to such qualifying child. (4) Determination of default trustee.--For purposes of selecting a trustee for an account established under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall take into account-- (A) the history of reliability and regulatory compliance of such trustee, (B) the customer service experience of such trustee, (C) the costs imposed by such trustee on the account or account beneficiary, and (D) to the extent practicable, the preferences of any individual described in paragraph (3)(A) with respect to such eligible individual. House 110116 pilot birth window and citizenship at birth: For purposes of subsection (a), the term eligible individual means an individual-- (1) who is born after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2029, and (2) who is a United States citizen at birth. House 110116 pilot return identification: (1) In general.--No credit shall be allowed under subsection (a) to a taxpayer unless such taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year-- (A) such individual's social security number, (B) if such individual is married, the social security number of such individual's spouse, and (C) the social security number of the eligible individual with respect to whom such credit is allowed. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). House 110116 pilot definitions: For purposes of this section-- (1) Qualifying child.--The term qualifying child has the meaning given such term in section 152(c). (2) TRUMP account; account beneficiary.--The terms `TRUMP account' and `account beneficiary' have the meaning given such terms in section 530A(b).. House 110116 improper-claim penalty and incorporated definitions: In the case of any taxpayer that makes an excessive claim for a credit under section 6434-- (1) if such excess is a result of negligence or disregard of the rules or regulations, there shall be imposed a penalty of $500, or (2) if such excess is a result of fraud, there shall be imposed a penalty of $1,000. (b) Definitions.--The terms `negligence' and `disregard' have the same meaning as when such terms are used in section 6662.. House new 25F allowance: (a) Allowance of Credit.--In the case of an individual, there shall be allowed as a credit against the tax imposed by this chapter for the taxable year an amount equal to the aggregate amount of qualified contributions made by the taxpayer during the taxable year. House own contributing-taxpayer credit limits: (b) Limitations.-- (1) In general.--The credit allowed under subsection (a) to any taxpayer for any taxable year shall not exceed an amount equal to the greater of-- (A) 10 percent of the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year, or (B) $5,000. (2) Allocation of volume cap.--The credit allowed under subsection (a) to any taxpayer for any taxable year shall not exceed the amount of the volume cap allocated by the Secretary to such taxpayer under subsection (g) with respect to qualified contributions made by the taxpayer during the taxable year. (3) Reduction based on state credit.--The amount allowed as a credit under subsection (a) for a taxable year shall be reduced by the amount allowed as a credit on any State tax return of the taxpayer for qualified contributions made by the taxpayer during the taxable year. House own eligible-student definition: (1) Eligible student.--The term `eligible student' means an individual who-- (A) is a member of a household with an income which is not greater than 300 percent of the area median gross income (as such term is used in section 42), and (B) is eligible to enroll in a public elementary or secondary school. House own complete calendar volume-cap mechanism: (g) Volume Cap.-- (1) In general.--The volume cap applicable under this section shall be $5,000,000,000 for each of calendar years 2026 through 2029, and zero for calendar years thereafter. Such amount shall be allocated by the Secretary as provided in paragraph (2) to taxpayers with respect to qualified contributions made by such taxpayers, except that 10 percent of such amount shall be divided evenly among the States, and shall be available with respect to individuals residing in such States. (2) First-come, first-serve.--For purposes of applying the volume cap under this section, such volume cap for any calendar year shall be allocated by the Secretary on a first- come, first-serve basis, as determined based on the time (during such calendar year) at which the taxpayer made the qualified contribution with respect to which the allocation is made. The Secretary shall not make any allocation of volume cap for any calendar year after December 31 of such calendar year. (3) Real-time information.--For purposes of this section, the Secretary shall develop a system to track the amount of qualified contributions made during the calendar year for which a credit may be claimed under this section, with such information to be updated in real time. (4) Annual increases.-- (A) In general.--In the case of the calendar year after a high-use calendar year, the dollar amount otherwise in effect under paragraph (1) for such calendar year shall be equal to 105 percent of the dollar amount in effect for such high-use calendar year. (B) High-use calendar year.--For purposes of this subsection, the term `high-use calendar year' means any calendar year for which 90 percent or more of the volume cap in effect for such calendar year under paragraph (1) is allocated to taxpayers. (C) Prevention of decreases in annual volume cap.--The volume cap in effect under [[Page H2305]] paragraph (1) for any calendar year shall not be less than the volume cap in effect under such paragraph for the preceding calendar year. (D) Publication of annual volume cap.--The Secretary shall make publicly available the dollar amount of the volume cap in effect under paragraph (1) for each calendar year. (5) States.--For purposes of this subsection, the term `State' includes the District of Columbia..
